items.title: VALCO expansion must be backed by Ghana-specific sustainability evidence – Corporate finance professional
items.description: Corporate finance professional, John Boafo, has urged the government to back its ambition to increase production at the Volta Aluminium Company Limited (VALCO) to at least 200,000 tonnes annually by the end of 2028 with credible, locally grounded sustainability evidence. The CFA Charterholder and Chartered Accountant says Ghana must demonstrate the commercial and environmental advantages of the smelter through verifiable data on its electricity sources, carbon emissions, production efficiency and community impact to strengthen its investment case. Mr Boafo argues that relying solely on international sustainability benchmarks could overlook Ghana’s specific economic, institutional and environmental circumstances, potentially limiting investors’ understanding of the project’s actual value. His comments come as the government pursues a strategic partnership to modernise and expand VALCO, with plans to increase annual production from about 40,000 tonnes to at least 200,000 tonnes by the end of 2028. In January 2026, the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, urged the selected investor to commence modernisation work immediately, while emphasising the importance of securing the investment needed to revive the smelter. The government subsequently inaugurated a negotiating team on August 21 to agree on the definitive terms of the proposed partnership. Finance professional and researcher, John Akwetey Boafo Mr Boafo’s concerns are informed by a systematic review of sustainable banking and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) integration research, which he led as first author and published in July 2025 in the Interdisciplinary Journal of Management Sciences. The study analysed 1,104 Scopus-indexed publications spanning 1933 to 2025 and identified significant gaps in research output from Africa and Latin America. The review found that Nigeria accounted for 12 publications and South Africa 19, compared with 141 for China and 129 for India within the dataset. It also identified limitations in the application of sustainability models developed in other markets, particularly where informal economies and state-owned institutions have different operating conditions. Mr Boafo says these gaps should prompt Ghana to develop its own evidence base as it negotiates the future of one of its strategic industrial assets. “The counts do not prove a financing penalty by themselves, and they are not a substitute for a Ghana-specific study. They establish something more fundamental: African conditions occupy a small share of the evidence used to refine sustainable-finance practice. “For a project as distinctive as VALCO, locally grounded evidence is therefore not an academic luxury. It is part of the investment case,” he said. Electricity and carbon emissions Mr Boafo identified electricity consumption as one of the critical areas where sustainability evidence could influence the assessment of VALCO’s competitiveness and investment potential. He noted that GIADEC’s original vision for VALCO was linked to the use of electricity from the Akosombo Dam to support an integrated aluminium industry. While hydroelectric power could give the smelter a lower electricity-related carbon footprint compared with facilities relying on coal-generated electricity, he said Ghana would need to establish the actual sources of power supplied to the plant. According to him, the historical association with hydropower should not be treated as sufficient evidence of the facility’s current environmental performance. He also drew attention to the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which entered its definitive phase on January 1, 2026, and covers aluminium imports. Under the current CBAM methodology, the calculation for aluminium includes direct emissions but excludes indirect emissions from electricity consumption, although such emissions are covered in the methodology for certain other sectors, including cement and fertilisers. Mr Boafo said the distinction was important because a lower electricity-related carbon footprint did not automatically translate into a lower carbon cost under every international regulatory framework. “Electricity is commonly the largest component of an aluminium producer’s carbon footprint, yet the current CBAM treatment of aluminium does not differentiate imports on the basis of electricity-related indirect emissions. “That does not erase the commercial value of hydropower. It means Ghana must demonstrate that value through verified carbon data, reliable power economics, buyer commitments and financing terms rather than assume that the border mechanism will recognise it automatically,” he said. He added that the government should ensure that environmental and sustainability claims made about VALCO are supported by measurable information that investors, lenders and prospective buyers can independently assess. ESG reporting and investment decisions Mr Boafo also highlighted inconsistencies in Environmental, Social and Governance ratings, noting that different rating agencies may arrive at varying assessments because of differences in their methodologies and the weighting assigned to specific indicators. He cited research examined in his review which found a highest correlation of 0.61 among the ESG rating agencies assessed, suggesting that their assessments were positively related but not entirely consistent. He said the differences reinforced the need for project-specific sustainability reporting that provides investors with access to underlying performance data rather than relying exclusively on composite ESG scores. His review also identified greenwashing as a continuing concern in sustainable finance, emphasising the importance of reliable disclosure and verifiable environmental claims. Evidence needed for VALCO’s expansion For Ghana’s aluminium ambitions, Mr Boafo believes the immediate priority should be to assemble a comprehensive evidence base that connects sustainability performance to the smelter’s commercial prospects. He proposed that this should cover traceable electricity sources, verified carbon emissions, production efficiency, environmental performance, workforce outcomes and the impact of operations on surrounding communities. “For VALCO, the immediate implication is practical. Ghana should build an investable evidence pack around the variables that make the project distinctive: traceable power sources, verified electricity-related emissions, production efficiency, environmental performance, workforce effects and community outcomes. “That evidence will not replace an investor’s analysis. It will ensure the analysis is built on Ghana’s actual conditions rather than on regional assumptions,” he said. He further argued that sustainability information should be connected to operating costs, production reliability, buyer requirements and financing assumptions to help investors assess the commercial value of the smelter’s potential advantages. Mr Boafo’s recommendations draw on his more than a decade of experience in corporate finance, including mergers and acquisitions advisory and business valuation, with experience supporting transactions across West Africa and the United States. While his research does not specifically assess VALCO or its proposed investment arrangements, he believes its findings provide a basis for examining the evidence required to finance sustainable industrial development in Ghana. He said the country’s ambition should be to ensure that the modernisation of VALCO is supported not only by the necessary capital and technology but also by independently verifiable evidence of its long-term economic, environmental and social value. Sources 1. Boafo, J. A., Maclean, E. O., Danzerl, N. O. P., & Amoafo-Danquah, K. P. (2025). Sustainable banking and ESG integration: A systematic review of green finance practices in global banking systems. Interdisciplinary Journal of Management Sciences, 2(1), a07. Published 28 July 2025. Table 1 and sections 3.2 and 3.3 report the dataset metrics and country distribution. The discussion sets out the methodological limitations and research recommendations. Full research article (PDF) | DOI: 10.38140/ijms-2025.vol2.1.07 2. Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation. GIADEC secures strategic investors for the modernization of VALCO and construction of alumina refinery. January 2026. Reports investor selection, the production target of at least 200,000 tonnes a year by the end of 2028, and the five evaluation pillars. GIADEC investor-selection announcement 3. Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation. Government inaugurates negotiations team for VALCO modernisation. 21 August 2026. Describes the team’s mandate to negotiate definitive terms and the smelter’s historical connection to the Akosombo power project. GIADEC negotiations announcement 4. LME Insight. How carbon costs have evolved to reshape aluminium pricing. 22 May 2026. Reports the industry estimate of 60 to 80 percent for electricity-related indirect emissions, depending on the power source. The estimate is not specific to VALCO. LME Insight article 5. European Commission. Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. Confirms that the definitive regime applies from 1 January 2026. European Commission CBAM overview 6. Regulation (EU) 2023/956, Article 7(1) and Annex II, as amended. Provides the legal basis for taking only direct emissions into account for the listed aluminium goods. Consolidated regulation, 20 October 2025

items.title: Justice : le reclassement des greffiers dans la hiérarchie A se précise
items.description: Les greffiers et administrateurs de greffe concernés par le reclassement dans la hiérarchie A pourront déposer leurs demandes à partir du jeudi 5 novembre 2026. La mesure, issue du protocole d’accord signé avec les syndicats de la Justice en août 2025, reste toutefois soumise à une démarche individuelle. Le processus de reclassement des greffiers et des administrateurs de greffe dans la hiérarchie A entre dans une nouvelle phase. Dans un communiqué conjoint, le ministère de la Fonction publique, du Travail et de la Réforme du Service public et le ministère de la Justice annoncent l’ouverture, à partir du jeudi 5 novembre 2026, du dépôt des demandes de nomination ou de reclassement des agents concernés. Cette mesure découle du protocole d’accord signé le 7 août 2025 entre le Gouvernement, le Syndicat des travailleurs de la Justice (SYTJUST) et l’Union nationale des travailleurs de la Justice (UNTJ), dans le cadre du Pacte national de stabilité sociale pour une croissance inclusive et durable. Pour concrétiser cet engagement, une formation de six mois a été organisée par le Centre de formation judiciaire (CFJ). À son terme, les attestations de réussite de l’ensemble des agents concernés ont été transmises au ministère chargé de la Fonction publique. Sur le plan réglementaire, un projet de décret modifiant le décret n° 2019-575 du 5 février 2019, relatif au statut particulier du cadre des fonctionnaires de la Justice, a été élaboré en concertation avec les parties prenantes. Le texte a été examiné par le Conseil supérieur de la Fonction publique lors de sa séance du 7 juillet 2026, avant sa transmission au Secrétariat général du Gouvernement pour la poursuite de la procédure. Les deux départements ministériels indiquent que l'examen des situations administratives des agents fait ressortir des perspectives d'amélioration de leur niveau hiérarchique et de leur indice, avec des incidences positives attendues sur leurs rémunérations et leurs pensions de retraite. Toutefois, le Gouvernement précise que le reclassement ne sera pas automatique. Chaque agent remplissant les conditions requises devra formuler une demande expresse. Les intéressés devront ainsi adresser une demande au ministre de la Fonction publique, du Travail et de la Réforme du Service public, accompagnée d'une copie légalisée du diplôme de fin de formation délivré par le CFJ. Par ailleurs, les autorités indiquent que le maintien, dans la nouvelle hiérarchie, du grade détenu antérieurement par l'agent ne peut être accordé au regard de la législation actuellement applicable. Une telle disposition risquerait, selon elles, de créer un précédent et de fragiliser les règles encadrant la gestion des carrières dans la Fonction publique.

items.title: Sahara marocain: les membres des deux Chambres du Parlement saluent hautement le contenu du communiqué du Cabinet Royal et les efforts diplomatiques du Royaume
items.description: Les membres des deux Chambres du Parlement ont salué hautement, lundi, le contenu du communiqué du Cabinet Royal du 30 octobre, publié à l'issue de la réunion du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU sur la question du Sahara marocain ainsi que les efforts déployés par la diplomatie marocaine pour clore définitivement ce conflit artificiel. Lors d'une séance plénière conjointe des deux Chambres, les intervenants ont souligné que la teneur du communiqué marque un passage stratégique décisif de la logique de la gestion du conflit à la transformation radicale de ses paramètres et de ses règles vers la clôture définitive du dossier. Ils ont considéré que la non reconduction du mandat de la MINURSO, 35 ans après sa création, constitue une étape historique mettant fin à sa présence sur le terrain, saluant le ferme attachement du Royaume au cessez-le-feu et sa détermination à défendre sa souveraineté, son intégrité territoriale et la quiétude de ses citoyens. Les parlementaires ont également été unanimes à souligner la centralité de la Vision Royale Clairvoyante dans la transformation radicale que connait le dossier du Sahara marocain, notant que la Diplomatie Royale marquée par la pertinence de la vision et constance des positions, la consolidation des acquis ainsi que par la construction des alliances sous le prisme de l'intégrité territoriale a permis d'élargir le cercle des reconnaissances et du soutien international croissant à l'initiative d'autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine. Dans ce sillage, ils ont relevé que le vote de 11 pays en faveur du dernier projet de résolution reflète le soutien international grandissant à la position marocaine. Cette dynamique couronne le processus consacré par la Résolution du Conseil de Sécurité des Nations Unies 2797 (31 octobre 2025), qui coïncide avec l'institution du Roi Mohammed VI de la Fête de l'Unité, ont-ils souligné, réaffirmant que ledit processus érige l'initiative d'autonomie en base exclusive et unique pour le règlement du différend, avec le soutien de plus des deux tiers des États membres des Nations Unies et de puissances mondiales. Les intervenants ont insisté sur la nécessité de consolider les acquis diplomatiques et les avancées en matière de développement réalisés par le Royaume, en poursuivant le renforcement de la cohésion nationale et du front intérieur, ainsi qu'en consacrant la justice spatiale et sociale. Par ailleurs, les députés et conseillers des deux Chambres ont appelé l'Algérie à assumer ses pleines responsabilités juridiques et humanitaires face à la situation tragique des personnes séquestrées dans les camps de Tindouf, rappelant à cet effet, la politique de la « main tendue » du Royaume, visant à tourner la page de ce différend et à mettre fin aux souffrances de ces séquestrées en facilitant leur retour à la mère Patrie. Ils ont également affirmé que la position nationale ne cesse de se renforcer sur le terrain grâce à l'élan de développement global que connaissent les Provinces du Sud, à la faveur du Nouveau modèle de développement dédié à ces régions, dont le Roi Mohammed VI a donné le coup d'envoi en 2015. Dans ce contexte, ils ont rappelé les grands projets structurants, tels que la Voix express Tiznit-Dakhla, le Port Dakhla Atlantique, le Projet de Gazoduc Africain Atlantique, ainsi que l'Initiative Royale favorisant l'accès des pays du Sahel à l'Océan Atlantique. Dans le sillage de ce consensus national inébranlable autour de la marocanité du Sahara, les différentes composantes du Parlement ont exprimé leur profonde estime, fierté et admiration à l’adresse des membres des Forces Armées Royales, de la Gendarmerie Royale, de la Sûreté Nationale, des Forces Auxiliaires, de la Protection Civile et de l’Administration Territoriale, saluant leur dévouement sans relâche pour la défense de l’intégrité de la Patrie ainsi que la préservation de sa sécurité et de sa stabilité, sous la Sage Conduite du Roi Mohammed VI. The post Sahara marocain: les membres des deux Chambres du Parlement saluent hautement le contenu du communiqué du Cabinet Royal et les efforts diplomatiques du Royaume appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JUSAG says strike continues despite progress in talks with Judicial Service management
items.description: The Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has maintained its strike despite what it describes as progress in discussions with the Chief Justice and management of the Judicial Service over its outstanding demands. The association says it will only consider ending the industrial action after receiving a revised and improved approval from the government that addresses its concerns. In a statement signed by its General Secretary, Abdulai Yakubu, JUSAG said its leadership and that of the Senior Staff Association of the Judicial Service of Ghana (SSAJUG) held a meeting with the Chief Justice and management following the declaration of the strike. According to the association, the meeting was productive, with management expressing commitment to working with the government to address the outstanding demands. JUSAG also disclosed that it had sighted a revised letter from the Ministry of Finance concerning the payment of allowances. It said management had further agreed to present the outstanding issues to the Office of the President for expedited resolution. While commending the Chief Justice and management for their interventions, the association said it would await the outcome of the discussions before its National Executive Council (NEC) takes a decision on the next steps. However, it stressed that the latest developments had not resulted in the suspension of the strike. “We wish to inform staff and the public that THE STRIKE IS STILL ON,” the statement emphasised. JUSAG added that it would communicate any change in the status of the industrial action after receiving a revised and improved government approval that satisfies its demands. Government approves arrears payment The latest developments follow a November 2 letter from the Ministry of Finance approving payment of ten months’ salary and allowance arrears for Judicial Service staff and members of the Lower Court Bench. The approved arrears are to be paid in two instalments, with the first covering January to May 2026, scheduled for November, and the second covering June to October 2026, expected in December. The approval was communicated in a letter signed by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, directing the Controller and Accountant-General to give effect to the payment arrangement. Meanwhile, the strike has disrupted activities at several court premises across the country, including the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Accra Circuit Court and some District Court offices, with security personnel restricting access. Despite the disruption, the Office of the Judicial Secretary has announced that the Supreme Court will convene for its normal court business on Tuesday, November 3, following a directive by the Chief Justice.

items.title: INEC pledges inclusive voting for PwDs
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has pledged to strengthen electoral accessibility for persons with disabilities (PwDs) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission said it would provide assistive materials, improve polling unit accessibility and train electoral officials to ensure inclusive participation. Gombe State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Alhaji Umar Gajiram, gave the assurance on Monday during a sensitisation workshop in Gombe. Gajiram, represented by the Administrative Secretary, Hajiya Fadimatu Bakari, said every Nigerian deserved equal opportunities to participate in democratic processes. He stressed that disability should never prevent eligible citizens from exercising their constitutional voting rights. According to him, INEC recognises that persons with disabilities have equal rights and that their votes, voices and contributions matter. He said the commission was implementing measures to remove barriers preventing PwDs from participating fully in elections. These include providing assistive materials, ensuring accessible polling units, training electoral officials and collaborating with disability organisations. Gajiram stressed that disability inclusion must be integrated into every electoral activity rather than treated as an additional responsibility. “Disability inclusion should not be treated as an additional responsibility but as an important part of our work,” he said. He urged Disability Desk Officers (DDOs) to maintain regular engagement with PwDs and communicate their challenges to the commission. He also encouraged participants to speak openly about their experiences and recommend improvements to electoral arrangements. “As we look forward to 2027, our goal is simple: to ensure that no eligible Nigerian is left out of the electoral process because of disability,” he said. He said INEC wanted wheelchair users to access polling units easily and visually impaired voters to receive appropriate assistance. Similarly, he said, persons with hearing impairments should have access to election information, enabling every eligible voter to participate with dignity and confidence. Also speaking, Gombe State Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPwD), Mallam Gambo Ahmad, commended INEC for organising the workshop. He described the arrangements as exceptional compared with previous engagements, particularly the provision of accessible communication materials. Ahmad specifically appreciated INEC for providing Braille materials for visually impaired participants and an interpreter for effective communication. He said the arrangements ensured participants could understand the discussions and contribute meaningfully to the proceedings. He identified intellectual disabilities, hearing impairments, physical disabilities, visual impairments, spinal cord injuries and leprosy-related disabilities among conditions represented in Gombe. Others, he said, included persons with albinism, adding that people with different disabilities remained members of the same community. “We are all part of this community, although we face different challenges,” Ahmad said. He, however, urged INEC to ensure adequate representation of persons with disabilities among its temporary electoral personnel during the elections. Ahmad said many PwDs possessed the necessary qualifications and capacity to serve in different electoral positions. “Some can serve as electoral officers, while others can perform different supporting roles,” he said. He argued that employing PwDs in election administration would encourage greater participation and strengthen public confidence. According to him, seeing persons with disabilities administering elections would demonstrate INEC’s commitment to genuine inclusion. Ahmad urged the commission to sustain and strengthen its disability inclusion initiatives beyond the 2027 general elections. Also, the Gombe State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Hajiya Maimuna Abubakar, commended INEC for organising the workshop. She described the initiative as an important step towards promoting justice and equal opportunities for persons with disabilities. Abubakar maintained that electoral participation was a fundamental right, not a privilege. She said every eligible Nigerian, including persons with disabilities, had the right to register, vote and participate in choosing national leaders. She encouraged PwDs not to isolate themselves because of their conditions but to register and participate actively in elections. The NOA director also pledged the agency’s readiness to collaborate with INEC in providing necessary information and support. She said the collaboration would help ensure persons with disabilities were adequately informed and equipped to participate in the electoral process. Vanguard News The post INEC pledges inclusive voting for PwDs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Govt slashes high-speed diesel price by Rs7.76 per litre, petrol by Rs3.40
items.description: The government on Monday slashed the price of petrol by Rs3.40 per litre, and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.76. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs374.51 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.20. The prices are applicable for Nov 3 (Tuesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. However, under a new arrangement , oil refineries would contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a monthly cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price on consumers’ end. “The [petroleum levy] impact on estimated total country volume of Rs. 14.71/litre shall be surrendered by refineries @ Rs49.02/litre on their sales to [oil marketing companies],” reads a document by Ogra. The government announced the arrangement during a press conference in Islamabad, held by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. “I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” Malik said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months. “They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that, we were able to maintain the price.” On Oct 27, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy. The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17 . For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then. Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene. Additional input by Khaleeq Kiani

items.title: Welfare Hub wins MoMo fintech bootcamp and hackathon in Kumasi
items.description: Three teachers from the Ashanti Region have emerged as zonal champions in the MoMo Fintech Lab Hackathon after developing a digital platform to automate welfare contributions and payments for workers’ associations. The team, known as Team Kasa, comprising Mohammed Salifu, Kamila Hassan and Mukhtar Al-Farouk, secured the Middle Belt zonal title with its prototype, Welfare Hub. The innovation aims to eliminate the challenges of manually collecting membership dues and distributing welfare funds, while promoting safer and more efficient digital financial transactions. Organised by MoMo Fintech, the bootcamp and hackathon provided participants with an opportunity to identify challenges within the digital financial ecosystem and develop practical solutions to address them. The initiative comes amidst the rapid growth of cybercrimes in digital financial sector, emphasizing the importance of the cyber protection for mobile money users and financial transactions. During the programme, participating teams worked on innovative ideas aimed at addressing challenges within the mobile financial services sector, with a focus on developing solutions that promote safer, more reliable and accessible digital financial transactions. Chief legal, regulatory affairs and reputation management officer at MobileMoney Fintech Limited, Papa Asai, stressed on the need for innovation, collaboration and technological advancement in addressing emerging threats within the digital financial space. Papa Asai highlighted the importance of equipping young people with the technical knowledge and problem-solving skills to respond to evolving digital security challenges. He encouraged participants to move beyond identifying problems to developing solutions capable of making a meaningful impact on society. After rigorous stages of the competition, Welfare Hub, led by Mohammed Salifu alongside Kamilu Alhassan and Farouk Muftahu Mohammed, emerged the overall winner. Susu Vault, represented by Jeffrey Owusu Peprah and Godfred Owusu, secured the first runner-up position, while EaziPay, developed by Fosu Boateng Klinsman, Wedam Atigidiwe Prosper and Boahen Felix, finished in the third position. The three teams emerged from seven finalist projects selected to showcase their ideas and solutions during the competition. The other finalist teams were Merchant ShiftBook, Athena Techne, QUEBE and FAMEK Campus. The bootcamp and hackathon form part of efforts to encourage young innovators to apply technology and creative thinking in addressing real-world challenges. By bringing together young talents to develop solutions to emerging digital financial threats, the programme highlighted the potential of innovation in strengthening confidence and security within Ghana’s growing digital financial ecosystem.

items.title: 'Over a million' abuse images found on phone of UK man who drugged, raped wife: prosecutor
items.description: A man who drugged and raped his wife over two decades and allegedly invited strangers to participate had “over a million photographs and videos” on his phone cataloguing the abuse, a UK court heard on Monday. The court in Manchester, northwest England, is hearing the trial of nine men accused of various sexual offences against a woman who was abused by her husband — a man in his 60s who cannot be named to protect the victim’s identity. The husband filmed and shared images of the abuse on the “internet and social media applications” with “other like-minded men”, prosecutor Louise Oakley told the court. Some of the defendants allegedly “hid behind a screen” and conspired with the husband over the years to administer substances to the woman so she could be “used and abused”. And starting 2023, the prosecutor said, the husband began inviting men around to their home and filmed himself and others raping her while she was unconscious. It is the second case involving a man accused of inviting strangers to take part in abusing his wife currently being heard in Britain. A trial in Winchester in the south involving four men opened last week. Global awareness of the crime, known as organised drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA), has grown following the high-profile conviction in France of Dominique Pelicot , who drugged and raped his then-wife Gisele for nearly a decade alongside strangers. Oakley told the jury in Manchester that the husband’s phone, which was seized when he was arrested, was like a “confession booth” including “barbaric sexual fantasies” going back to 2004. “There were over a million photographs and videos cataloguing not only his abuse of his wife but abuse on her committed by others, including those in the dock today,” Oakley said. “There is no doubt he lived a double life masked in respectability,” the prosecutor said. The husband pleaded guilty in September to some 60 sexual offences against his wife, including administering a substance with intent to stupefy or overpower her. He and 13 other men are accused of conspiring to abuse the woman. Four of the men have since pleaded guilty to various offences. The remaining nine men, aged between 28 and 70, deny various charges including rape, sexual assault and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent. They include a taxi driver, a recruitment agency worker, a building supplies worker and a senior medic.

items.title: Chief of Staff pledges Government support as JICA marks 50 years of training Ghanaian professionals
items.description: The Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has expressed the Government’s wish to continue supporting the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) training program, as the agency marks 50 years of building the capacity of Ghanaian officials and professionals. Julius Debrah gave this assurance when the Chief Representative of the JICA Ghana Office, Takayuki Uchiyama, led a delegation of senior government officers, all former participants of JICA training, on a courtesy call to Jubilee House. The visit aimed to formally inform the Chief of Staff of the 50th anniversary, present the program’s achievements, and seek the Government’s support for activities marking the milestone. Five decades of shared knowledge The first Ghanaian participants travelled to Japan for JICA training in 1976. Since then, more than 5,000 Ghanaian officials and professionals have taken part, and more than 150 have earned master’s and doctoral degrees at Japanese universities. Speaking at the meeting, the Chief of Staff noted that the knowledge, experience and work ethic Ghanaians have gained in Japan are important to the nation’s development. He affirmed that the Government would continue to support the program in the years ahead. Mr. Uchiyama said the true value of the program lies in its lasting effect on people and institutions: “For fifty years, JICA training has been about capacity building of people, and its effects last far beyond the training itself. The knowledge and skills that more than 5,000 Ghanaians have brought home from Japan continue to shape institutions and are passed on to colleagues and the next generation. This is how training lays a lasting foundation for Ghana’s stable development. We look forward to building on it together over the next fifty years.” A program that has grown, deepened and widened Over five decades, JICA training in Ghana has evolved in several important ways: Growing: The alumni network has expanded steadily to more than 5,000 Ghanaians. Deepening: The program has moved from short courses to full university degrees. Ghanaians have pursued master’s degrees in Japan under the JDS scholarship since 2012 and the ABE Initiative since 2015. More inclusive: The participation of women has more than tripled, from about 1 in 8 participants in 1976–94 to about 4 in 10 in 2020–25. Training now reaches regional and district officials as well as national ministries. Broad in reach: Participants come from six sectors central to Ghana’s development: health, agriculture, industry and tourism, education, governance and planning, and infrastructure and energy. Health and agriculture lead the way. Stronger after COVID-19: Training moved online during the pandemic so that learning never stopped. In-person training in Japan resumed in 2022 and has grown strongly since, and the number of new degree scholars has more than doubled compared with before the pandemic. Anniversary activities As part of activities to mark this milestone, JICA will hold a symposium to celebrate 50 years of training in Ghana. The event will bring together alumni, government partners, and stakeholders to reflect on the program’s impact and chart the course for the next 50 years of cooperation between Ghana and Japan. JICA will announce symposium details in due course. About JICA training in Ghana JICA’s training program takes Ghanaian officials and professionals to Japan and partner countries to share knowledge and experience in areas important to Ghana’s development. It includes short-term courses through the Knowledge Co-Creation Program (KCCP), a training scheme linked to JICA technical cooperation projects, Master’s and Doctoral degree programs at Japanese universities, including the JDS scholarship and the ABE Initiative. Alumni remain connected through the JICA Alumni Association of Ghana (JAAGHA).

items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Comedian and preacher Woli Arole has appealed to those involved in the burial dispute surrounding late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, to allow him a befitting burial, urging them to end what he described as unnecessary public arguments. Arole made the appeal in a video shared on Instagram on Monday, describing the late singer as a great talent whose death had left friends and colleagues grieving. “I want to speak on behalf of Toluwanisings’ demise, and this is what God asked me to say. We’ve lost a great guy, a great gift to a generation. Even we, his friends and colleagues, have not recovered. For some of us, he is so close to us, and his death is really painful. A big elephant has gone,” he said. He also criticised people he accused of using the controversy to attract attention on social media, saying public discussion should instead focus on Toluwanisings’ wife and children. “It’s saddening and sad that a lot of people are now beginning to want to start to use it as a means for social media traction. You are m***. I have a right to say it. A young man had died in almost his prime, and the discussion is not even about the wife left behind and two kids? No. What you want to start doing is unlicensed, ungoverned, unnecessary talk, interviews and nonsense. A lot of people speaking about him this way never spoke about him while he was alive, about his music, please, please,” Arole said. He urged those involved to let the burial arrangements proceed and allow the singer to be laid to rest with dignity. “This is why it is a burden in my spirit, and I have to speak, and this is what the Lord is laying in my heart. The Bible says: Let the dead bury their dead. Whatever process, anything that needs to be done within that corner, let it be done. Let the young man be given a befitting burial,” he said. View this post on Instagram Woli Arole added that the burial dispute could not erase the singer’s musical legacy and called on the public to support his family and preserve his work through his children. “Nobody can ruin his legacy; he lived a good life, please. He sang songs that are eternal; his songs rang in our hearts. Whichever way he is buried, Toluwanisings is in our hearts forever; his sound is forever. So, please, I want to beg us in the name of Jesus, you should focus our energy on what is left: how his legacy will be preserved in his children and the wife,” he said. He concluded: “God bless Toluwanisings’ legacy, God bless his wife and his children, let the noise and unnecessary nonsense die down in the name of Jesus.” Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026, but did not disclose the cause of death. The singer’s burial arrangements have drawn public attention following disagreements over where he should be laid to rest. Vanguard previously reported that a family representative rejected a cemetery burial and threatened to exhume the singer’s remains if he were buried there. His paternal grandmother also said she opposed a cemetery burial and wanted him buried at his home. items.title: Affaire du Pr Rachid Cherkab : le procès reporté au 16 novembre à Casablanca
items.description: La Chambre criminelle près la Cour d’appel de Casablanca a décidé, ce lundi 2 novembre 2026, de reporter l’examen de l’affaire impliquant le médecin anesthésiste et réanimateur Rachid Charkab, un technicien ainsi qu’un autre médecin du CHU Ibn Rochd. La prochaine audience est fixée au 16 novembre, afin de permettre à la défense de préparer ses arguments. Lors de cette audience, les avocats ont présenté des demandes de mise en liberté provisoire en faveur du professeur et des autres personnes poursuivies dans ce dossier. La séance s’est déroulée en présence de plusieurs acteurs syndicaux et associatifs, ainsi que de patients ayant bénéficié des soins du médecin au sein du CHU Ibn Rochd. À l'issue de l'audience, l'avocat et militant des droits humains Mohamed El Ghalloussi a pris la parole devant la presse. Il a notamment exprimé son soutien au professeur Charkab, estimant que son arrestation pourrait être liée à des tensions avec certaines parties qui auraient attendu une occasion pour lui porter préjudice. Il a également évoqué la plainte déposée par l'administration de l'établissement hospitalier. L'avocat a par ailleurs appelé à la mise en liberté provisoire du médecin, mettant en avant sa réputation professionnelle et son engagement humanitaire auprès de ses patients. Il a estimé que son maintien en détention constituait un risque, tout en appelant à lutter contre la corruption et l'enrichissement illicite. Pour rappel, le tribunal correctionnel d'Aïn Sebaâ, à Casablanca, avait condamné en première instance le professeur Rachid Charkab à un an de prison ferme. Dans le même dossier, une deuxième personne avait écopé de deux ans de prison ferme, assortis d'une amende de 5.000 dirhams. Un technicien avait, quant à lui, été condamné à six mois de prison ferme et à une amende de 1.000 dirhams. Le report de l'audience au 16 novembre ouvre ainsi une nouvelle étape dans cette affaire, dans l'attente de l'examen des demandes de la défense et de la suite de la procédure judiciaire. The post Affaire du Pr Rachid Cherkab : le procès reporté au 16 novembre à Casablanca appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Energy Commission Renewable Energy Challenge: Government urged to fund TVET students to develop renewable energy prototypes
items.description: There are heightened calls for the government to prioritise funding for students in the technical and vocational education and training sector to develop more innovative prototypes and contribute to sustainable energy solutions in Ghana. The appeal was made during the seventh edition of the Energy Commission Renewable Energy Challenge held in the Ashanti Region. Technical students from various senior high schools in the northern and southern part of the country showcased innovative prototypes designed to address the country’s renewable energy needs. Head of Public Affairs at the Energy Commission and coordinator of the Renewable Energy Senior High School Challenge, George Sarpong, said inadequate funding remained a major obstacle hindering the development of students’ projects. He called on the government and other stakeholders to provide financial support for research, prototypes development and scaling up of students’ innovations. “Usually, the challenge has to do with funding because it is a huge project and a huge competition that brings senior high schools onto one platform to develop renewable energy solutions. The students have to raise money to conduct research and build prototypes, so we need support,” he said. Mr. Sarpong disclosed that participating schools spend approximately GH¢35,000 to develop its prototype, underscoring the financial demands of the competition and the need for sustained investment. At the zonal level, Ahantaman Girls’ Senior High School emerged winner of the southern zone, while Dabokpa Senior High Technical School won the northern zone competition. The students appealed to the relevant ministries and authorities to support and scale up their innovations to make them accessible to communities, particularly rural farmers. “We are calling on the various ministries to support and scale up our projects. With adequate funding, these innovations can be extended to farmers in rural areas, especially considering that agriculture employs more people than the government sector,” they said. Professor Francis Kermanson of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), who was a judge for the competition, commended the students for their creativity and innovation. He noted that their works demonstrated Ghana’s potential to advance renewable energy solutions. However, he stressed the need to address funding challenges facing technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions to enable students to develop more sophisticated prototypes. “The challenges facing TVET schools need to be addressed to help them develop even better prototypes. I am very impressed with what I have seen so far from the technical schools,” he said. The grand finale of the Energy Commission Renewable Energy Challenge is expected to take place in Accra, where the zonal winners will compete for the national title.

items.title: Rent Control orders UGEL, private hostel operators to refund excess rent by November 17
items.description: The Rent Control Department (RCD) has directed the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL) and all private hostel operators across the country to suspend rent increases that have not undergone the required legal assessment and refund excess rent paid by affected tenants by November 17, 2026. The directive, issued on November 2, 2026, requires affected operators to immediately restore previous rental rates and stop collecting increased rents until the applicable assessment process has been completed and statutory requirements satisfied. The Department said the decision followed a petition from the University of Ghana Students’ Representative Council (UGSRC), seeking a review of proposed residential fees by UGEL. Following the petition, the Rent Control Department requested clarification from UGEL. After considering the matter, the Department extended the directive to all private hostel owners and operators nationwide. The RCD maintained that private hostel accommodation falling within the scope of Ghana’s rent laws is subject to its regulatory oversight, stressing that describing premises as student accommodation or a private hostel does not automatically exempt operators from complying with rent legislation. Under the directive, operators are required to maintain previous rental rates until the necessary assessment and statutory procedures for implementing revised rents have been completed. The Department has also ordered operators to refund the difference between the previous rental rate and the increased amount actually paid by affected tenants. The refund exercise is expected to run from November 3 to November 17, 2026, with operators required to identify affected tenants, calculate excess payments and provide documentary evidence of refunds for verification. However, the Department clarified that refunds will cover only the difference resulting from the increased rental rates and will not include original rent payable under previous arrangements or separate legitimate charges unrelated to the increases. The RCD has also warned hostel operators against intimidating, threatening, harassing or victimising tenants who question rent increases, seek refunds or report suspected violations. It further cautioned against using threats of eviction, denial of accommodation or other unlawful means to compel tenants to accept unassessed increases or abandon complaints. The Department said it would conduct inspections, examine tenancy and payment records, verify refunds and investigate complaints as part of its monitoring and enforcement measures. It cited provisions of the Rent Act, 1963 (Act 220), including sections 25(1)(b), 25(1)(i), 26(1) and 27(1), warning that operators found to have contravened the law could face the prescribed legal consequences. The directive applies not only to UGEL and University of Ghana-affiliated accommodation facilities but also to all private hostel owners and operators nationwide whose accommodation falls within the scope of applicable rent laws. The Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, signed the directive, which was issued by Sylvia Kenou, Head of the Corporate Affairs and Communications Unit of the Rent Control Department. The Department has urged all affected operators to comply immediately, warning that failure to suspend unassessed rent increases and refund excess payments by November 17 could attract enforcement action in accordance with the law

items.title: US to exclude S. Africa, Rwanda from Africa duty-free trade deal
items.description: The United States Trade Representative on Monday said Washington would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from a major Africa-US duty-free trade deal, a blow to both economies, over practices “inconsistent” with the deal’s eligibility criteria. “These concerning and pervasive practices include, but are not limited to, barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region,” Jamieson Greer said in a statement. The exclusions will take effect from January 1, the statement said. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which grants eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential access to the US market, has been renewed until the end of 2028, but is reviewed annually. South Africa is the program’s largest beneficiary but its eligibility has come under scrutiny as Washington steps up criticism of Pretoria, including false allegations of discrimination against white Afrikaners that South Africa rejects. On Thursday, South Africa’s trade minister said the country hoped for a favorable decision from Washington on the issue, arguing that continued market access would be in the best interest of both countries. A little over a week earlier, however, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the country should “prepare” for an adverse decision. The US president reviews countries’ eligibility for AGOA annually. Any removal requires 60 days’ notice to Congress and the country concerned. South African Trade Minister Parks Tau told reporters in Johannesburg last week that regardless of Trump’s decision on AGOA, his country’s economy would remain stable as it seeks other international markets. – Increasing pressure on Rwanda – Washington has been increasing economic pressure on Rwanda over its alleged backing of the armed M23 rebel group in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. Last week, the United States sanctioned the Rwandan defense ministry over those ties, which the Rwandan government denies. With Rwandan help, the M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC — home to valuable minerals coveted by world powers — since it took up arms again in 2021. Rwanda’s foreign minister told AFP last week that his country should not be a “scapegoat” for events in DR Congo. “The situation in the DRC, the political situation, the security situation, is mainly a Congolese issue,” Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told AFP on the sidelines of a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow before the US sanctions were imposed. “Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever,” he added. items.title: Nigerians, others to face 10-yr wait for UK permanent residency
items.description: United Kingdom, UK has revised its proposed immigration reforms, retaining plans to double the waiting period for most migrants seeking permanent settlement from five to 10 years while exempting hundreds of thousands of care workers from the extended requirement. The revised policy, announced on Monday, follows opposition from trade unions and members of the governing Labour Party over the potential impact of the changes on low-paid foreign workers, particularly those employed in the care sector. The British government had initially proposed last year that lower-skilled foreign workers should wait between 10 and 15 years before qualifying for permanent residency, officially known as indefinite leave to remain. However, under the revised arrangements, hundreds of thousands of care workers will be exempt from the longer waiting period, retaining a five-year route to settlement, subject to eligibility requirements. The exemption is significant for Nigerians working in Britain’s health and social care sector, which relies on foreign workers to fill staffing shortages. Despite the concessions, the reforms will still double the standard qualifying period for permanent settlement from five to 10 years. The changes, expected to take effect next year, will also apply retrospectively to migrants already living and working in Britain. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the revised policy was designed to reward migrants who contribute to British society while imposing tougher conditions on those who violate immigration rules. “Those who contribute most will settle fastest,” Mahmood said. “Those who don’t play by the rules ‌will be refused or wait longer.” Under the new rules, migrants earning at least £50,271 annually and certain skilled public-sector workers will be eligible to apply for permanent settlement after five years, while those earning more than £125,000 can qualify after three years. Meanwhile, refugees who entered Britain illegally, particularly those who arrived by small boats, will face significantly longer waiting periods, potentially extending to decades. The government estimates that despite the exemptions, the reforms will reduce by 500,000 the number of migrants who arrived in Britain from 2021 and would otherwise have qualified for permanent settlement by 2030. As many as 1.4 million migrants are still expected to qualify within the same period under the revised arrangements. items.title: Art Africa Gallery spotlights women’s struggles, breast cancer awareness through ‘She Carries the Market’ exhibition
items.description: Art Africa Gallery has held the fourth edition of its Colour Cure exhibition, using art to spotlight the responsibilities women bear in society and raise awareness about breast cancer. The exhibition, themed She Carries the Market , features works by seven female artists – Abena Oyiwaa, Betty Acquah, Vicki Adoe, Fauziya Fliege, Serene Kalme, Nyornuwofia and Charity Derby Akeiti – as well as documentary photographer Ask Photos. The works explore the often-overlooked labour, resilience and experiences of women. Speaking on behalf of the gallery, Partner Manager and co-curator, Henry Kwaku Duah, said the initiative was established by Ghana’s Ambassador to South Korea, Kojo Choi, to amplify women’s stories, support female artists and promote breast cancer awareness. He said this year’s theme draws inspiration from Makola Market, where women traders and kayayei carry heavy physical loads while shouldering responsibilities that extend beyond their livelihoods. “Sometimes, we see women only from the outside and fail to recognise what they carry within. From the market to the home and the workplace, women bear responsibilities that deserve greater appreciation,” he said. Mr Duah said the theme was intended to resonate with all women, including those balancing formal employment with childcare and household duties. He urged the public to visit the gallery and purchase artworks, noting that a portion of sales would support breast cancer awareness through Sonotech Medical Centre. He said the exhibition also benefited from partnerships with Samsung, PaySwitch Company Limited, Data Bloom Africa and other organisations, which he hoped would help build a lasting community around art and breast cancer advocacy. Co-curator Sarah Emefa King, known as Sasa, said the exhibition was personal, having witnessed breast cancer affect members of her family and participated as an artist in Colour Cure two years ago. She praised the eight exhibitors for bringing distinct perspectives to the theme, from the raw realities documented by Ask Photos to the expressive paintings of established artists Betty Acquah and Vicki Adoe, alongside emerging voices. “Each artist brings something different. Photography captures the realities around us, while painting allows us to imagine possibilities beyond hardship. Together, these works show that women cannot be confined to one image or expectation,” she said. Documentary photographer Ask Photos said her participation was a way of contributing to breast cancer advocacy, stressing that the disease could affect anyone. “I feel people sometimes believe sickness will never touch them. But cancer could absolutely affect me, too. By contributing a percentage of my art sales, I can support the work being done in breast cancer awareness,” she said. Veteran artist Betty Acquah, exhibiting at Colour Cure for the fourth time, said her three works reflected women’s strength and determination. Her piece Balancing Act draws on the agility and resilience of kayayei who carry heavy loads, sometimes without using their hands to steady them. “I wish I could give more towards breast cancer awareness. For now, we are contributing a percentage of sales, and I hope we can do more in the future,” she said. For first-time exhibitor Abena Oyiwaa, a self-taught artist who has painted for five years, the inspiration lies in the invisible labour and social pressures women endure. Her work explores the tension between society’s expectations around education, marriage and motherhood and women’s personal aspirations. “I want to show the beautiful chaos of being a woman, especially an African woman, and what we go through beyond our appearance and what people see,” she said. The exhibition brought together the CEO of PaySwitch Company Limited, Mr Aaron Demenu; the Ambassador of Japan to Ghana; the spouses of the Turkish and Danish ambassadors to Ghana; and other artists. The exhibition opened to the public on October 24 and is scheduled to run for one month, through November 23, 2026.

items.title: Fraude avec l’IA : un jeu d’enfant (par Abdou Khadir Seck)
items.description: L'histoire tient en quelques lignes, rapportées par le quotidien L'Observateur. Un cadre de l'APROSI est accusé d'avoir fabriqué de toutes pièces de faux certificats médicaux avec ChatGPT, pour tromper sa direction et masquer des manquements professionnels. L'agence a découvert le pot aux roses et saisi la Section de recherches de Colobane. L'enquête dira ce qu'il en est, et la présomption d'innocence vaut pour lui comme pour tout le monde. Mais cette affaire pose une question qui nous concerne tous. Hier, pour obtenir un faux certificat médical, il fallait un complice, un médecin véreux et un faussaire habile. Il fallait du temps, de l'argent et des risques à prendre. Bref, tout un dispositif huilé et rompu à la tâche. Aujourd'hui, il suffit juste d’un téléphone, d’une connexion internet et le tour est joué en quelques secondes. Frauder ne coûte presque rien. « C’est une dinguerie » pour parler comme les jeunes. Certificat médical, attestation, facture , diplôme, justificatif d'absence : l'IA peut produire des documents d'un réalisme bluffant. Signature, cachet, en-tête : ce qui demandait autrefois la main d'un faussaire est devenu un jeu d'enfant que l’on peut à partir de quelques prompts. Certes, certaines IA refusent encore de toucher aux pièces sensibles. Mais d'autres sont nettement moins regardantes. Rien de nouveau sous le soleil, diront certains. Depuis la nuit des temps, les fraudeurs s’emparent de chaque technologie nouvelle : la photocopieuse, le scanner, Photoshop. C'est vrai. Mais cette fois, la différence est de taille : l'outil est à portée de main de tous, sans aucun savoir-faire. Et cela ne coûte presque rien. Personne n'est à l'abri. Et malheureusement nos administrations se modernisent à pas de tortue. Beaucoup en sont encore au papier tamponné, à la photocopie « certifiée conforme » et au cachet qu'on examine à l'œil nu. Un système pensé pour une époque où falsifier était difficile. Face à l'IA, il devient une passoire. Le fraudeur dribble, et la vieille défense regarde passer le ballon. La solution n'est pas d'interdire l'IA. Elle est de moderniser : documents numériques vérifiables par QR code, échanges directs entre structures de santé et employeurs, signature électronique, agents formés à repérer les faux. Ce n'est pas un luxe. C'est une urgence. Dans cette affaire, la supercherie a été démasquée. Tant mieux. Mais combien d'autres passent entre les mailles du filet sans que personne ne s'en aperçoive ? Quand frauder devient un jeu d'enfant, il est temps que nos administrations se mettent à jour. Ps : cette chronique a été corrigée par une IA

items.title: NUPRC opens bidding for 40 oil, gas blocks Nov 20
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has announced that bidding for 40 oil and gas blocks under its 2026 licensing round will commence on November 20. The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this on Monday during a roundtable discussion at the 2026 ADIPEC Exhibition and Conference in Abu Dhabi. The discussion was titled, “Energy Sovereignty in an Interconnected World: Aligning National Priorities, Markets and Global Security.” In a statement by the Commission, Eyesan urged international investors to take advantage of opportunities in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, saying improved security, attractive fiscal terms and incentives had made the country more competitive. She said the Commission would open its bid portal on November 20 and expressed optimism that the investment conditions would attract interested investors. “We are expecting investors to turn to Nigeria. We are going in for another licensing round and we will be launching our bid portal on November 20. We expect to see interested investors because the environment is a lot more competitive. “We have set a very attractive fiscal framework for investors. The entire environment is a lot more secure. We have been able to manage costs with a lot of incentives for investors and we expect to see investors take up the offer when we open the portal,” she said. Eyesan attributed the improvement in Nigeria’s investment climate to the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), enacted in 2021, and executive orders signed by President Bola Tinubu. She said the Commission had conducted at least four successful licensing rounds between 2021 and 2026, attracting investments into the country’s oil and gas industry. According to her, the development marked a departure from the pre-PIA era, when licensing rounds were less frequent, adding that the reforms had strengthened Nigeria’s competitiveness in attracting upstream investments. On the country’s gas potential, Eyesan said Nigeria had an estimated 215 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves but was producing barely seven billion cubic feet per day, leaving significant opportunities for investors. She said recently completed and planned gas infrastructure projects would help unlock supplies, improve domestic availability and position Nigeria to serve regional and international markets. Eyesan cited the Nigeria-Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline and the Trans-Sahara Gas Pipeline as two major projects being considered to transport gas to regional markets and Europe. She said the projects, alongside other infrastructure developments, would help Nigeria meet domestic demand and supply gas to other markets. The NUPRC chief executive noted that global competition for investment had intensified as more countries discovered petroleum resources and sought to attract international capital. She said Nigeria was addressing concerns investors consider before committing funds, including execution risks, operating costs, project delays and policy uncertainty. “We understand that investors will prize execution risk, cost, delays and also uncertainty and so what we have done in Nigeria is to ensure that we guard against these risks and then attract the investment required to enable us unlock the huge resources we sit on,” she said. The post NUPRC opens bidding for 40 oil, gas blocks Nov 20 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UG to expand student accommodation as 2026/27 freshmen matriculate
items.description: The University of Ghana says it is pursuing measures to expand on-campus accommodation as it welcomes fresh students for the 2026/27 academic year. The announcement comes as the university holds its matriculation ceremony across five sessions for its four colleges and the Accra City Campus. Speaking on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor, Provost of the College of Humanities, Professor Joseph Awetori Yaro, said the university recognises the growing demand for on-campus accommodation and is taking steps to address the challenge. He said management was pursuing sustainable measures to increase the number of available bed spaces and improve the student residential experience. “The university recognises the growing demand for on-campus accommodation,” Professor Yaro said. He added that management was “actively pursuing sustainable measures to increase accommodation capacity and improve the student residential experience.” The accommodation challenge remains a concern for students seeking residential facilities on campus, as demand continues to put pressure on available spaces. Meanwhile, the new student representative, Benedicta Lartey, an LLB student, highlighted some of the difficulties freshmen encountered during the registration process. She said some students experienced delays and had to wait for long periods while moving between offices to obtain the information they needed. “For some of us, registration involved waiting long hours, moving from one office to another, and struggling to obtain the information needed,” she said. Ms Lartey appealed to university staff to provide timely information and exercise patience when assisting new students as they settle into university life. The university has also urged freshmen to observe its rules, maintain discipline and take responsibility for their conduct as they begin their academic journey.

17 abducted Kaduna worshippers died in captivity – CSW
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo No fewer than 17 worshippers abducted during an attack on churches in Ariko community, Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State, reportedly died in captivity, while eight others were released after spending five months with their abductors, Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW), Nigeria, has disclosed. The Chief Executive Officer of CSW Nigeria, Rev. Dr Yunusa Nmadu, disclosed this during a presentation at ECWA Goodnews Church, Kaduna, to mark the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church (IDOP). Nmadu said the victims were among 37 worshippers abducted when gunmen attacked three churches in the community during Sunday services on April 5, 2026. He said 12 of the abducted worshippers escaped at different times, while 17 died in captivity and eight were eventually released. Speaking on the theme, “Light in the Darkest Places,” the CSW chief executive also disclosed that 11 people were abducted in Awon village, also in Kachia LGA, on April 20, 2026. According to him, one of the victims escaped, six were confirmed dead, while four others remained in captivity six months after their abduction and were reportedly in critical condition. He also recalled the abduction of 177 worshippers from three churches in Kurmin Wali, Kajuru LGA, during Sunday services on January 18, 2026. Nmadu said the government initially denied the incident but later acknowledged it following interventions by organisations, including CSW. He said the victims were eventually released after spending 18 days in captivity. The CSW chief executive described the incidents as part of a disturbing pattern of attacks, killings and mass abductions across Kachia, Kajuru, Kauru, Kagarko and other parts of Kaduna State, which he said had forced thousands of residents to flee their ancestral communities. He expressed concern that persistent insecurity had restricted freedom of worship in several affected communities, leaving some Christians unable to attend church services without fear of attacks or abduction. Nmadu alleged that Christians constituted about 99 per cent of victims in several affected communities, adding that religious activities had become increasingly difficult in settlements facing persistent security threats. He also raised concerns over the alleged treatment of abducted victims, particularly women and children, who he said were subjected to sexual violence, starvation and other inhumane conditions. According to him, male and female captives were separated into different camps, where their movements were restricted and access to basic necessities, including drinking water, controlled by their abductors. He alleged that some women, including nursing mothers and elderly women, were repeatedly sexually assaulted, while some who regained their freedom reportedly returned home pregnant. He added that captives sometimes spent several days without food and had limited access to soap and other basic hygiene materials. Nmadu also drew attention to the continued captivity of Leah Sharibu, who was abducted in February 2018, describing her case as a reminder of the prolonged ordeal of people held because of their Christian faith. He further alleged that in some parts of the North-East, Christian passengers were singled out and abducted during attacks on commercial vehicles, while passengers of other religious backgrounds were allowed to go. Calling for greater solidarity with victims of religious persecution, Nmadu urged Christians to remember those in captivity and support efforts to secure their freedom. He said CSW had worked in Nigeria for more than 17 years to promote freedom of religion or belief through documentation of human rights violations, support for victims and survivors, training of human rights defenders and engagement with government institutions. “Behind every report and every statistic is a person: a widow, a child, a pastor, a family who has lost a home or a loved one. They are not numbers to us. They are our brothers and sisters, and when one part of the body suffers, we all suffer with it,” he said. He urged Christians to remain steadfast in their faith and show solidarity with persecuted believers, drawing inspiration from John 1:5, which says that the light shines in darkness and the darkness has not overcome it. items.title: GRIDCo to construct 5th feeder in Kumasi for improved power reliability
items.description: Kumasi is set for a major boost in electricity supply as the Ghana Grid Company (GRIDCo) moves to complete the construction of a fifth feeder by the end of the year. This critical intervention is expected to ease pressure on the existing network and improve power reliability for more than 1.5 million households and businesses across the Ashanti Region. A high-level delegation from the Ghana Grid Company and the Electricity Company of Ghana, together with the Ashanti regional minister, inspected ongoing power upgrade projects in the Ashanti Region. At the Ridge substation, the team assessed the progress of work on the installation of a new higher-capacity transformer to meet the growing demands for electricity supply. The replacement of the new transformer of 145mVA capacity is prompting the construction of a new feeder, which GRIDCo says would add 80 megawatts of power supply in Kumasi. “We are working to add a fifth feeder. This would add to the transformer and increase the capacity to serve demand. And we project by December that work would be done. “This would add an additional approximately 80MW capacity to the existing substation at Ridge,” Chief Executive Officer of GRIDCo, Ing Frank Asirifi Otchere, said. The upgrade of a 161kV transmission line from Anwomaso to Ahodwo is progressing steadily, with engineers currently stringing sixty towers between the two substations. “We thought to increase the capacity of the lines that connect Anwomaso to Ridge to enable more power to flow. The old-line circuit was about 360 mW capacitor. “The new line is approximately 1000 mW capacitor. This would increase the capacity of the infrastructure in Kumasi. The contractor has completely decommissioned the whole transformer and its towers,” Ing. Otchere added. In collaboration with the Electricity Company of Ghana, the ongoing power infrastructure upgrades are expected to cause a month-long intermittent and localized power cuts. But the power providers maintain the exercise is necessary to improve reliability of power supply to the region. Meanwhile, power consumers are being assured of timely and effective communication on planned outages to minimise disruptions and align them for the acute shortage. Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene noted a joint team from the power providers, information service department and the regional coordinating council, will be deployed to relay communication on the planned outage across affected communities.

items.title: Allemagne : des enfants retrouvent des clous, des aiguilles ou des agrafes cachés dans leurs bonbons d’Halloween
items.description: C'est un Halloween particulierement sordide que de jeunes Allemands et leurs familles ont vecu cette annee. Ces 1er et 2 novembre, nombre de medias allemands se font l'echo de signalements d'« objets metalliques » retrouves dans les bonbons collectes par des enfants au soir du 31 octobre. Dans le land de Bade-Wurtemberg, une aiguille a ete trouvee dans des bonbons, selon un signalement effectue le 1er novembre au commissariat de police de Filderstadt. « Il s'agit du troisieme cas » dans cette ville situee au sud de Stuttgart, ont souligne des medias locaux. En Basse-Saxe, la police de Rotenburg a indique qu'une fillette de neuf ans s'etait blessee a la langue apres avoir mordu dans une barre chocolatee contenant une epingle d' au moins cinq centimetres . En Baviere, un autre enfant de neuf ans, ayant fait du porte-a-porte a Munich, a mordu dans un chewing-gum piege avec un clou . Selon la police, l'enfant a recrache sans se blesser. Une aiguille de couture de trois centimetres de long a ete trouvee dans une barre chocolatee par une fillette de 11 ans a Burg, dans le land de Schleswig-Holstein. Dans celui de Thuringe, a Umpferstedt, c'est une agrafe metallique qui a ete retrouvee dans un chewing-gum, selon la police, ainsi qu' un hamecon dans un bonbon mou recupere par une fillette de 10 ans. En Amerique du Nord, cette « pratique » – qui selon certains tiendrait de la « legende urbaine » – est redoutee par les parents depuis des decennies. Dans les medias americains et canadiens , des cas ont ainsi ete rapportes cette annee encore. Une famille de Columbus, dans le Nebraska, a ainsi trouve une aiguille dans une barre Snickers en rentrant de la collecte de bonbons d'Halloween a rapporte WMTV. Dans le meme etat du centre, un clou d'environ 2,5 cm a ete retrouve plante dans une barre chocolatee a Scottsbluff, a rapporte la Nebraska Rural Radio Association. Meme chose a Crystal City, au Texas, ou une epingle aurait ete retrouvee dans une barre chocolatee ou encore a Waukegan, dans l'Illinois, ou des epingles a cheveux et du fil de fer ont ete retrouves dans des bonbons. Dans l'Indiana, la police de Corydon a rapporte qu'un enfant avait trouve une aiguille dans une barre chocolatee lors d'une collecte de bonbons dans un camping a Birdseye.
