items.title: Rachida Brakni : « Les Maghrébins sont traités comme des citoyens de seconde zone »
items.description: Quand Rachida Brakni prend la parole sur le racisme en France , c'est pour faire entendre un cri de colère. Dans le contexte de la montée de l’extrême-droite, de la banalisation du racisme et du passage à l’acte de certains extrémistes, l'actrice d’origine algérienne a pris la parole. Ses mots pour dénoncer la stigmatisation et l'essentialisation sont forts. Rachida Brakni : « Les musulmans de France désignés comme l’ennemi de l’intérieur » Celle qui est l'épouse de l'ancien footballeur Éric Cantona s’est exprimée dans le magazine Télérama. Alors que certains médias et politiques sont désignés comme étant les véritables responsables de la violence extrémiste, comme l’attentat de Trappes de vendredi 23 octobre, Rachida Brakni dénonce une « obsession distillée en continu sur les chaînes d’infos » qui désignent les musulmans de France comme « l’ennemi de l’intérieur ». Cela finit par devenir, pour beaucoup, « une vérité », à force d'entendre de tels propos. Si Rachida Brakni monte régulièrement au créneau pour dénoncer le racisme, c’est aussi parce que l'essentialisation transcende les générations et semble interminable pour elle et pour tous ceux qui ont des origines étrangères, particulièrement musulmanes et africaines. « Quand va-t-on enfin nous considérer comme des Français à part entière ? » « Jusqu’à la combientième génération va-t-on conserver le suffixe ‘d’origine’ ? Et quand va-t-on enfin considérer que nous sommes des Français à part entière ? », s’écrie-t-elle, dénonçant que les Maghrébins de France soient vus par certains comme « des citoyens de seconde zone, comme au temps de la colonisation ». Pour décrire son ressenti dans la France d'aujourd'hui, elle utilise une métaphore très forte, évoquant un « enfant de parent maltraitant », qui s'y « accroche désespérément », mais qui constate que « d'un point de vue psychique, c'est ravageur ». « La société doit faire ce travail de mémoire pour que l'on puisse avancer tous ensemble », dit-elle à propos du lourd héritage de la guerre d’Algérie. La comédienne a sorti l’été dernier son premier roman, « La part absente », et a entamé en ce début novembre la tournée de la pièce « Médée/s ». Sa dénonciation du racisme est un vieil engagement, né dans sa condition d'enfant immigré algérien. Un engagement né dans le comportement de l’administration avec son père analphabète En juin 2022, elle a raconté à Mme Figaro avoir vite développé un rapport aigu à l'injustice en voyant le comportement de l’administration à l'égard de son père analphabète. Comme elle n’entendait pas chez les politiques ce qu’elle attendait, elle a envisagé de devenir avocate, estimant que « le droit est un rempart ». Elle a finalement opté pour une carrière artistique. Ce qui ne lui a pas fait perdre de vue son engagement. Au contraire, elle a fait de sa visibilité un outil pour donner un meilleur retentissement à son combat contre le racisme. Femme de caractère, elle a refusé en juillet dernier la Légion d’honneur qui lui était attribuée par l’Élysée, expliquant que son honneur à elle « se situait ailleurs ». L’article Rachida Brakni : « Les Maghrébins sont traités comme des citoyens de seconde zone » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: CBN appoints eight agents for crude oil exports
items.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has appointed eight Pre-Shipment Inspection Agents (PIAs) to monitor the country’s crude oil and gas exports. The appointments were announced in a circular issued by the Director of Trade and Exchange at the apex bank, Aderinola Shonekan, dated October 28, 2026, and published on the CBN website. The appointed agents include Trexem Energy Services Limited, assigned to Egina, Qua-Iboe and Tuja terminals; and Dakee Engineering and Construction, which will cover LNG, Escravos (Gas), Bonny River Terminal and EGTL. Others are Geospace Limited, assigned to Escravos, Odudu and Crawthorne; 617 Limited, covering Bonga, Brass and Usan/Eae; Robinson Energy International Limited, assigned to Ugo-Cha, Pennington, Oyo Aje, Ima and Nembe; and Trobell International Nigeria Limited, covering Forcados, Bonny and Okwori. Integrated Shipping Services was assigned Akpo, Antan, Okoro, Anyala-Madu and Ebok, while Nephron Business Limited will cover UK Politics, Staple, Yoho, Abo, Agbami, Ajakpa, Okono, Okwok and additional marginal field streams designated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). The CBN also appointed two Monitoring and Evaluation Agents (MEAs) to supervise the activities of the PIAs. They are Q&Q Control Services and Arlington Security Services. The circular was addressed to authorised dealer banks, the Nigeria Customs Service, terminal operators, the NUPRC, the Nigerian Midstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited and oil and gas companies. The appointments took effect from the date of the circular, October 28, 2026. The post CBN appoints eight agents for crude oil exports appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UNICROSS in turmoil as ASUU resumes strike after 104-day suspension
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, University of Cross River State (UNICROSS) chapter, on Monday, resumed its strike after 104 days, accusing the government of failing to honour agreements that ended the last one. The chapter Chairman, Dr Patrick Ushie, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard in Calabar, said the decision to resume the strike was taken at a union meeting today (Monday) following the government’s failure to honour agreements that led to the suspension of the industrial action on July 21, 2026. His words: “It is true that we have resumed the strike we initially called off on July 21 following a series of meetings with the government and its representatives. “However, certain agreements reached before the suspension have not been implemented as agreed by the government. “They have not only breached the timelines for implementation but have also failed to respond to our notices. “This time around, we are not going to suspend or call off the strike until our grievances are addressed,” he said. Recall that the UNICROSS chapter of ASUU embarked on an indefinite strike on May 19, 2026, over welfare concerns and the non-implementation of agreements reached with the union’s national body. The union had listed 11 demands as the basis for the industrial action, including the implementation of the salary structure and other welfare benefits of academic staff. Other demands included the immediate implementation of the non-financial components of the 2025 ASUU-Federal Government renegotiated agreement and increased government funding for the university. The union also demanded prompt payment of monthly salaries not later than the third day of each succeeding month. It further called for the payment of outstanding salaries and arrears of the 35 per cent and 25 per cent wage awards implemented in public universities since January 2023. The union also demanded the remittance of outstanding check-off dues owed to ASUU-UniCross and its national body since 2017, amounting to N11.9 million, as well as deductions for December 2024 and November 2025. Other outstanding demands included the payment of promotion arrears and earned academic allowances accrued between July 2011 and December 2017 under the 2009 Federal Government-ASUU agreement. items.title: NDDC denies bridge collapse report in Bayelsa
items.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) has dismissed reports circulating on social media that a bridge project under construction in Otuogori community, Ogbia Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, had collapsed. The Commission said an incident occurred at the construction site of the 600-metre Otuogori-Otuegwe Bridge, but insisted that the bridge itself had not been constructed and therefore could not have collapsed. Addressing journalists during an inspection of the project, the NDDC Director, Bayelsa State Office, Engr. Godknows Alamieyeseigha, described the reports as misleading. “We don’t have a bridge yet because we are still at the stage of crossing the beams. So, no bridge has collapsed. “However, there was an incident at the construction site, and we are assessing the circumstances surrounding what happened,” he said. Alamieyeseigha dismissed suggestions that the incident resulted from structural failure, describing it as an accident during construction. He expressed confidence that the construction company would address issues identified during the assessment and complete the project. He also said no bridge had collapsed in Bayelsa State or any of the nine Niger Delta states. The NDDC director said the Commission’s current board and management, led by Chairman Chiedu Ebie and Managing Director, Dr Samuel Ogbuku, had prioritised quality assurance in project execution. He added that NDDC engineers and independent consultants regularly inspected project sites across the region to ensure compliance with approved engineering designs and standards. Also speaking, the Managing Director of the construction firm, Mr Christian Emiezor, assured that the Otuogori-Otuegwe Bridge was being executed in line with high construction standards. He explained that the project was still at the preparatory stage, with work focused on positioning the beams before the construction of the main bridge structure. According to him, the incident occurred during the launching of the beams, which were being positioned on their bearings. “We are constructing a 600-metre bridge, but as you can see, we have not constructed a bridge yet. What you are seeing is just preparations for the bridge,” Emiezor said. He described the incident as a minor accident, explaining that a beam resting on a bearing but not yet secured could slide during the positioning process. “What was going on was the launching of the beams, and in the process, there was a slight accident. Because the beam was resting on a bearing and had not been secured, it could slide. That was what happened,” he said. Emiezor added that safety measures at the site prevented casualties. “The good thing is that, with the safety measures put in place, no life was lost,” he said. The post NDDC denies bridge collapse report in Bayelsa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ICU-Ghana urges sustained breast cancer awareness beyond October
items.description: The Industrial and Commercial Workers’ Union (ICU-Ghana) has urged Ghanaians to sustain breast cancer awareness efforts beyond October, emphasising the importance of early detection and timely medical intervention. The union says awareness campaigns should go beyond the annual Breast Cancer Awareness Month to encourage people to speak openly about the disease, seek medical advice and support those affected. Speaking at a breast cancer awareness programme organised in collaboration with Ibis Styles Hotel in Accra on Thursday, October 29, ICU-Ghana General Secretary Morgan Ayawine said the initiative represented a partnership aimed at raising awareness, promoting early detection and saving lives. He described breast cancer as a major health concern that affects not only patients but also their families and communities. “However, we are assured that early detection and timely medical intervention can significantly improve treatment outcomes and save lives,” he said. Mr Ayawine expressed concern that many women continue to suffer in silence because of fear, stigma and inadequate information about the disease. Under the theme of breaking the silence, he urged women to become more conscious of changes in their breasts, seek appropriate clinical screening and consult health professionals promptly when they notice unusual symptoms. “Today, we must send a clear message: no more silence! Early detection matters,” he said. He cautioned women against allowing fear or stigma to prevent them from seeking medical attention, urging them to make their health and well-being a priority. The ICU-Ghana General Secretary also highlighted the fact that men can develop breast cancer, calling for awareness campaigns to include both sexes. He encouraged men to support women by urging them to seek medical advice and participate in appropriate screening. Mr Ayawine paid tribute to breast cancer survivors, describing their courage and resilience as a source of inspiration to others affected by the disease. “Your courage, resilience, and determination remind us that there is hope, even in the face of a breast cancer diagnosis,” he said. He further argued that healthcare must remain a national priority, saying the country’s development ambitions should be matched by efforts to protect the health of its people. “We cannot continue to talk about building a nation without prioritising the health of human beings who constitute the greatest assets of a nation,” he added. Breast Cancer Awareness Month is observed every October to promote public education, encourage early detection and support people affected by the disease. ICU-Ghana’s collaboration with Ibis Styles Hotel forms part of its efforts to promote the health and well-being of workers and the wider Ghanaian population. The union has called for continued public education, open conversations about breast cancer and greater support for survivors and people undergoing treatment.

items.title: Nii Noi earns Gospel Radio Show Host of the Year nomination at Praise Achievement Awards
items.description: Host of HitzPraiseZone on Hitz 103.9 FM, Nii Noi, has earned a nomination for Gospel Radio Show Host of the Year at the Praise Achievement Awards. The nomination recognises his work in gospel broadcasting, particularly his use of radio to promote gospel music, explore Christian teachings and engage listeners on matters of faith. Through HitzPraiseZone, Nii Noi hosts conversations centred on Christianity, biblical teachings and gospel music, providing a platform for listeners to explore their faith and connect with messages of spiritual encouragement. The recognition also draws attention to the contribution of gospel-focused radio programming to Ghana’s broadcasting landscape, particularly in creating platforms for Christian expression and music. His nomination adds to the recognition surrounding HitzPraiseZone, which has also earned a nomination for Christian Radio Programme of the Year at the 2026 edition of the awards. The nominations place both the programme and its host among the contenders at this year’s ceremony, scheduled for December 13, 2026, at the African Regent Hotel in Accra. The fifth edition of the Praise Achievement Awards is being held under the theme “Honouring Greatness, Celebrating True Excellence”.

items.title: GIS trains 146 officers in weapon safety and armoury management
items.description: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) has trained 146 officers in weapon safety and armoury management as part of efforts to strengthen operational discipline, accountability and national security. The Comptroller-General of Immigration, Samuel Basintale Amadu, said the training was necessary to protect officers, safeguard state-owned weapons, prevent the loss of firearms and ammunition, and maintain public confidence in the Service. He was speaking at the opening of a two-day Weapon Safety and Armoury Management Seminar at the Ghana Immigration Centre of Excellence (GISCE) in Accra. Mr Amadu urged participants to apply the knowledge and skills acquired to improve practices within their respective commands, stressing that proper weapon management was fundamental to professionalism, discipline and operational readiness. The seminar, organised in collaboration with armoury management experts from the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF), the Ghana Police Service (GPS) and the Small Arms Commission of Ghana, brought together selected Regional and Sector Commanders. It focused on equipping the officers with practical skills in the safe handling, storage, issuance and tracking of firearms and ammunition. The Armorer General of the Ghana Police Service at the National Headquarters, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCOP) Isaac K. Asante, led sessions on critical armoury management procedures, drawing on his operational experience. He highlighted the risks associated with weak inventory controls, poor record-keeping and inadequate supervision of weapons. DCOP Asante urged the commanders to maintain accurate registers, conduct regular inspections and enforce strict procedures for the issuance and return of firearms and ammunition. He stressed that every weapon and round of ammunition must be accounted for and traceable to a responsible officer at all times. Lieutenant Colonel Frank Tetteh-Kumah, Commander of the 851 Ammunition and Explosives Ordnance Regiment of the Ghana Armed Forces, also took participants through standard operating procedures for military armoury management. He explained that the Armed Forces maintained strict systems for the receipt, storage, issuance, inspection, maintenance and disposal of weapons and ammunition. He encouraged the GIS to adopt relevant aspects of these systems, particularly in physical security, access control, documentation, routine audits and command-level accountability. He further urged the officers to treat armoury management as a continuous responsibility rather than an occasional administrative exercise. A delegation from the Small Arms Commission of Ghana, led by its Director of Operations, Emmanuel Felix Mantey, also facilitated sessions on stockpile management and firearm safekeeping. The sessions examined measures to prevent weapon diversion, restrict unauthorised access, improve storage conditions and ensure proper tracking of firearms throughout their lifecycle. The Head of Intelligence of the Ghana Immigration Service, Deputy Commissioner of Immigration (DCOI) Kwasi Opoku Apau, described the seminar as timely, particularly in view of the Service’s expanding responsibilities in border and national security. He said building officers’ capacity in weapon safety and armoury management was essential to the GIS’s ambition to become a model institution in migration and border management. The seminar is expected to improve compliance with weapon-safety procedures, strengthen supervision across Regional and Sector Commands, and promote greater accountability in the management of firearms and ammunition. The Ghana Immigration Service continues to undertake specialised capacity-building programmes in areas including border security, counter-terrorism, intelligence, investigations and crisis management. Through collaboration with the Ghana Armed Forces, Ghana Police Service and Small Arms Commission, the Service is drawing on inter-agency expertise to strengthen its internal systems, improve operational professionalism and support effective border management and national security.

items.title: Ayuso condecora al presidente de Chile, el ultraderechista José Antonio Kast: “Defendemos lo mismo”
items.description: Es una de las máximas distinciones que concede la Comunidad de Madrid. El Gobierno de Isabel Díaz Ayuso (PP) ha entregado este lunes la Medalla Internacional de la región al presidente de Chile, el ultraderechista y nostálgico del pinochetismo José Antonio Kast. La líder autonómica ya ha condecorado con ella a otros dos presidentes latinoamericanos, el argentino Javier Milei —que también se ubica en el espectro de la extrema derecha—, y el ecuatoriano Daniel Noboa —un político nítidamente derechista—, además de los dirigentes antichavistas venezolanos Juan Guaidó y Edmundo González. Kast, en su primera gira por Europa desde que asumió la presidencia en marzo, se convierte así en el quinto de la lista. “Personalidades diferentes que, por sus distintas circunstancias, representan la defensa de la libertad y el derecho de sus pueblos a dirigir su futuro”, ha defendido Ayuso. La oposición de izquierdas critica a la presidenta regional por “convertir” el reconocimiento en el “carné de la internacional ultraderechista”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Traditional leaders, MMDCEs culpable in galamsey – President of National House of Chiefs
items.description: The President of the National House of Chiefs, Ogyeahoho Yaw Gyebi II, says some traditional leaders and MMDCEs are thwarting efforts to fight illegal mining through their active participation in the menace. According to him, persons who have taken up MMDCE positions have continued with the illegality that existed under the previous administration. He revealed his office has caused the arrest of chiefs suspected to be involved in galamsey. “I have lived under the NPP and galamsey was there, especially a year or two before elections they allowed their people to do the mining. Right now, it is the NDC government in power, and the NDC people are doing the mining,” he said. “I caused the arrest of four of my chiefs because they were involved in illegal mining. They pleaded with me, and they signed bonds. MMDAs, I can tell you that some of you are involved in the galamsey business just as some Nananom,” he added. He said although the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) continues to wage war on illegal mining on river bodies and in forest reserves, little positive impact has been achieved. In some areas, miners have become emboldened, extending activities to previously untouched reserves. He called for the fight to be devoid of partisanship and to involve local communities. He warned traditional authorities to properly ascertain the lawful use of lands before allocation. “A grant of customary land must not be mistaken for a license to mine illegally. We have a proper licensing procedure to be followed. One of the critical issues confronting our communities is the misuse of customary lands for activities that cause extensive environmental degradation such as illegal mining,” he stressed. Ogyeahoho Yaw Gyebi II was speaking as chair of the National Conference for MMDCEs on Illegal Small-Scale Mining organised by the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs. The conference brought together MMDCEs and some Regional Ministers to discuss illegal mining and how the local government ministry can help address the menace. Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, admitted the culpability of MMDCEs, noting that even failure to act makes them complicit. “It is not only when you are directly actively involved in mining that you are part of the problem. You can be part of the problem because you have seen people actively mining and you have looked the other way,” he said. He said it was time his ministry and MMDCEs took keen interest in combating the illegality. “When I became Minister, I decided that I am going to move into the fire and join my brother Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah so that if the fire is coming in the area of galamsey I also take part of it,” he added. The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources welcomed the support from the Local Government Ministry, proposing that MMDCEs help identify illegal mining hotspots, threatened water bodies and abandoned pits and take action. The Ministry charged MMDCEs to go after perpetrators to reclaim destroyed lands. Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, called for coordinated efforts to deal with the canker. Meanwhile, the Ashanti Regional Minister, speaking on behalf of MMDCEs, called for dedicated funding for the fight, noting that the District Assemblies Common Fund already has specific areas of allocation. The MMDCEs also called for prior notice when NAIMOS visits their areas to enable them to manage possible security situations. They cited uncoordinated security operations undertaken without their consent, trust deficits, lack of dedicated funding for the anti-galamsey fight, and the need to decentralise reclamation programmes to provide alternative livelihoods for miners.

items.title: NFA launches Cinema Train to boost Ghanaian film industry
items.description: The National Film Authority (NFA) has launched the Cinema Train Initiative, a new platform aimed at expanding access to cinema, improving film exhibition and creating sustainable revenue opportunities for Ghanaian filmmakers. Launched on Saturday, October 31, at Silverbird Cinemas in Accra, the initiative seeks to revive the country’s cinema-going culture by connecting filmmakers, distributors, cinema operators and audiences through a common platform. It is expected to address some of the challenges confronting the local film industry, particularly limited access to cinema facilities, inadequate exhibition opportunities for filmmakers and difficulties in generating revenue from their productions. Making films accessible CEO of NFA, Kafui Danku Speaking at the launch, the Chief Executive Officer of NFA, Kafui Danku, said the initiative was developed in consultation with key industry stakeholders to establish a more accessible and commercially sustainable film exhibition system. She said many Ghanaian filmmakers invested months, and sometimes years, in producing films that struggled to reach audiences because of limited exhibition opportunities. “We cannot build a sustainable film industry if we produce films without creating pathways for people to watch them. So, that is why we are launching the CinemaTrain initiative today,” she said. She explained that the initiative went beyond screening films to creating an ecosystem in which producers could earn from their work, distributors could connect content to markets and exhibitors could attract audiences. A key component of the initiative is the CinemaTrain digital platform, www.cinematrain.com, which allows users to discover available film screenings and purchase tickets. The platform is intended to simplify access to cinema screenings and make it easier for audiences to watch films on the big screen. Expanding cinema access The Authority also plans to expand cinema exhibition centres through partnerships with industry stakeholders, the private sector, public institutions and communities. The CEO said engagements with the National Commission on Culture, including visits to its centres, formed part of efforts to identify suitable spaces that could be developed into cinema exhibition points, particularly in communities with limited access to such facilities. She, however, stressed that the initiative’s success would depend on public participation and urged Ghanaians to support the cinema industry by purchasing tickets and attending screenings. “Buying a ticket is very important. We can all start by buying a ticket, watching a movie and encouraging somebody else to do the same,” she said. She also called on corporate organisations, sponsors and investors to support the initiative, saying their involvement would create more opportunities for exhibitors and strengthen the commercial prospects of the Ghanaian film industry. NFA targets one per cent of population For his part, the NFA Board Chairman, Mr Ivan Quashigah, reaffirmed the Authority’s commitment to strengthening the film industry, particularly by addressing longstanding challenges in the distribution and exhibition of Ghanaian films. He said the Cinema Train Initiative aligned with the Authority’s broader target of getting one per cent of Ghana’s population to patronise local films. The platform seeks to bring four key groups in the film industry onto one track: producers, distributors, exhibitors and audiences. Film producers, including Shirley Frimpong Manso and Ampong Kwaku Kwakye of Kornerstonez, pledged their support for the initiative. Representatives of cinema operators and exhibitors, including Silverbird Cinemas, Ozone Cinemas and The Trust Sports Emporium Limited, also expressed their support. Audiences can currently purchase tickets through the CinemaTrain website to watch No Man of God, directed by Ampong Kwaku Kwakye; Shirley Frimpong Manso’s Agency for the Dead; and Joseph, an African-Caribbean drama. The initiative is expected to provide more Ghanaian productions with access to audiences while creating opportunities for filmmakers and other industry players to generate revenue from their work.

items.title: More jobs, better pay: The budget Ghanaian workers deserve
items.description: Sustainability Consultant and Lecturer As Ghanaians await the presentation of this year’s national budget, expectations are understandably high. Reports suggest that job creation will be a major focus, offering hope in a country where unemployment and underemployment continue to affect millions, particularly young people. Yet many citizens approach the budget with cautious optimism. The challenge before the government is not simply creating jobs. The challenge is creating enough jobs while ensuring that workers earn incomes that allow them to live with dignity. For years, unemployment has remained one of Ghana’s most pressing socio-economic concerns. Every year, thousands of graduates leave universities, technical institutions, and vocational centres in search of opportunities that are often difficult to find. Many others remain trapped in informal employment, short-term engagements, or low-productivity activities that offer little security and limited prospects for growth. While successive governments have introduced employment initiatives, the demand for decent work continues to outstrip available opportunities. However, unemployment is only one side of Ghana’s labour market challenge. The other side is the growing number of workers who are employed but poorly paid. Across the country, many people wake up each day, faithfully report to work, and contribute to the growth of businesses and the economy, yet struggle to meet their basic needs. Rising prices of food, transportation, rent, healthcare, education, and utilities have significantly increased the cost of living, leaving many working families under considerable financial pressure. The current national daily minimum wage of GH₵21.70 illustrates this reality. For a worker employed over a standard 25-day working month, this amounts to approximately GH₵542.50 , or about GH₵547.50 by some calculations. The question policymakers must ask themselves is simple: can any worker realistically maintain a decent standard of living on less than GH₵550 a month in today’s economy? For many households, the answer is clearly no. Such income levels leave little room for savings, emergency expenses, children’s education, or long-term financial security. As a result, many Ghanaian workers find themselves in a troubling paradox. They have jobs but remain economically vulnerable. Employment, which should be a pathway to prosperity and social mobility, has become for many merely a struggle for survival. A budget that focuses only on the number of jobs created without considering the quality of earnings risks overlooking this important reality. This year’s budget therefore presents a unique opportunity to address both challenges simultaneously. Ghana needs policies that generate sustainable employment opportunities while improving wages and living standards. A successful jobs agenda should not be measured solely by employment statistics but also by the ability of workers to afford a decent life from the fruits of their labour. A bold review of the national minimum wage should therefore be a key component of the budget. Incremental increases that are quickly eroded by inflation are no longer sufficient. What is required is a significant upward adjustment that reflects prevailing economic conditions and the true cost of living. Such a move would not only improve the welfare of workers but also demonstrate a commitment to inclusive economic growth. Admittedly, concerns about the impact of higher wages on businesses are legitimate. However, the solution cannot be to maintain wage levels that perpetuate hardship among workers. Government can complement wage reforms with measures such as tax incentives, access to affordable financing, productivity enhancement programmes, and targeted support for small and medium-sized enterprises. Economic growth is strongest when businesses succeed and workers share fairly in the benefits. Indeed, higher wages can contribute positively to economic growth. Workers with increased disposable income spend more on goods and services, creating demand that supports local businesses and stimulates economic activity. Stronger purchasing power translates into healthier domestic markets and can help drive further job creation. Ultimately, the success of this year’s budget will be judged not only by how many jobs it promises but by how effectively it improves the lives of ordinary Ghanaians. The unemployed need opportunities. Workers need better pay. Families need relief from the mounting pressure of rising living costs. As the Finance Minister prepares to present the budget, Ghanaians will be looking beyond projections and policy statements. They will be looking for practical solutions to the challenges they face every day. A budget that confronts both unemployment and low wages head-on would send a powerful message that economic growth must be matched by improved livelihoods. The choice before policymakers is clear. Ghana does not simply need more jobs. Ghana needs more jobs, better pay, and a renewed commitment to the dignity of work.

items.title: Hashim mobilisers take 2027 campaign to rural North-West
items.description: …Accord candidate’s supporters target six million votes across seven states Mobilisers for the Accord Party’s presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, have extended their grassroots campaign to rural and underserved communities in Kano, Katsina, Kaduna and Jigawa states as part of a North-West mobilisation drive targeting six million votes. The campaign is moving beyond major towns and established political centres to engage residents of remote communities, including areas described by its organisers as ungoverned. The initiative is aimed at building a wider grassroots network across the states and taking Hashim’s message directly to communities often overlooked during conventional election campaigns. The rural outreach is part of a broader North-West mobilisation strategy announced by the Hashim Progressive Movement, which has set a target of six million votes across the region’s seven states: Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara. The current phase focuses on Kano, Katsina and Kaduna, often grouped by the campaign’s supporters as the KKK states, alongside Jigawa. According to the organisers, the mobilisation is intended to expand political engagement in communities with limited government presence and inadequate public services. Previous campaign activities have included the appearance of Hashim’s posters in parts of Kano, Kaduna, Katsina and Jigawa, as well as engagements with support groups and political stakeholders. In Jigawa, the Accord senatorial candidate, Aminu Aminu, had expressed confidence in Hashim’s ability to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the state. The organisers said the rural campaign would also provide an opportunity to engage communities on issues including insecurity, agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare and access to economic opportunities. With the 2027 general elections approaching, the campaign said it intended to pursue its six-million-vote target through wider grassroots participation and engagement beyond established political networks and urban centres. The post Hashim mobilisers take 2027 campaign to rural North-West appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Corruption : Ouahbi promet trois lois et un procès équitable
items.description: Pressé par les députés de sortir des textes contre l’enrichissement illicite et le conflit d’intérêts, le ministre de la Justice s’est engagé à les présenter, en plaçant la présomption d’innocence au cœur de leur rédaction. « Nous présenterons une loi sur l’enrichissement illicite, une loi sur le conflit d’intérêts, une loi sur le blanchiment d’argent. » L’engagement est signé Abdellatif Ouahbi, qui l’a pris ce lundi 2 novembre devant la Chambre des représentants, lors de la séance des questions orales où la lutte contre la corruption a occupé le devant de la scène. Le ministre de la Justice y a toutefois accolé une condition : ces textes devront être rédigés avec toutes les garanties d’un procès équitable. Plusieurs intervenants avaient réclamé la sortie des lois attendues en la matière. Ils ont appelé à revoir le système de déclaration du patrimoine, à mieux protéger les lanceurs d’alerte et à lier la responsabilité à la reddition des comptes. Certains ont plaidé pour l’application du principe « d’où tiens-tu cela ? », d’autres pour une loi sur le conflit d’intérêts conforme à l’article 36 de la Constitution et pour l’incrimination de la divulgation d’informations visant à obtenir des privilèges. Beaucoup ont aussi martelé que la seule voie répressive ne suffit pas : il faut y ajouter la prévention, la transparence, une application de la loi exempte de toute sélectivité et une volonté politique forte. Un député a même estimé que les dérives possibles doivent être traitées dans les textes proposés, et non invoquées pour s’y opposer, y voyant l’un des ressorts du discours populiste. Dans sa première réponse, le ministre avait tracé les contours de l’approche gouvernementale : application de la loi, respect de la présomption d’innocence, sauvegarde des droits et libertés. La lutte contre la corruption ne doit pas, a-t-il soutenu, devenir un prétexte pour s’affranchir des garanties. Il a récusé les pratiques populistes qui conduiraient à incarcérer des personnes sans respecter les règles de la loi, et relevé qu’il est aisé de multiplier les déclarations sur le sujet. Cette réponse a valu à Abdellatif Ouahbi les foudres d’Abdessamad Haiker, député du PJD, qui l’a qualifiée de « pitoyable ». L’élu a rappelé que la Constitution ne consacre pas seulement la présomption d’innocence et les garanties du procès équitable, mais aussi la bonne gouvernance, le lien entre responsabilité et reddition des comptes et l’interdiction des conflits d’intérêts. Selon lui, le retrait du projet de loi sur l’enrichissement illicite continuera de poursuivre le ministre. Piqué au vif, ce dernier a rétorqué par une question : « N’est-ce pas aussi de la corruption que de qualifier de “pitoyable” les propos d’un ministre ? » Tout en disant respecter le groupe du PJD, il a refusé que l’on franchisse les limites de la bienséance à son endroit, demandant s’il lui fallait quitter la séance pour éviter toute « misère » dans le débat. Après l’intervention du chef du groupe, Abdellah Bouanou, qui a demandé que le terme soit retiré du procès-verbal, le ministre a repris sa réplique. Il a alors souligné que l’enrichissement illicite est une question juridique, qui touche à la légitimité des sources d’une fortune, et non une occasion de préjuger de la richesse, de la propriété ou de la réussite économique. Il a invité les groupes à coopérer loin des surenchères pour élaborer des textes précis, conformes aux exigences du procès équitable, et s’est dit prêt à examiner les amendements et propositions de chacun. Sur le fond, Abdellatif Ouahbi a plaidé pour des pouvoirs assortis de garde-fous clairs. On ne fait pas confiance au pouvoir, a-t-il glissé : le législateur doit savoir à qui il confie des prérogatives pour pouvoir, demain, en demander compte. Il ne veut laisser aucun corrompu sans sanction, mais refuse tout autant de faire du tort à quiconque. Le défi consiste, a-t-il jugé, à concilier la lutte contre la corruption et la protection des fonctionnaires et des responsables contre l’arbitraire, afin qu’ils exercent leurs missions sans craindre une mise en cause non encadrée. Le ministre a ensuite insisté sur un danger qu’il juge sous-estimé : la condamnation sociale. Une simple convocation par la police ou une présentation devant la justice suffit, a-t-il averti, à faire d’une personne l’objet de jugements préconçus dans son entourage, avant toute décision judiciaire. Il a évoqué la photographie des suspects lors de leur interpellation et la diffamation que peut entraîner la diffusion de leur image : un non-lieu ou un acquittement n’efface pas nécessairement les dommages causés à la réputation et à la vie sociale. Certains citoyens, a-t-il ajouté, passent cinq ou dix ans devant les tribunaux avant d’être innocentés, d’où la question de la réparation et de l’indemnisation des erreurs judiciaires, et de l’entité qui doit en assumer le coût. À propos de l’enrichissement illicite, le garde des Sceaux a érigé la présomption d’innocence en colonne vertébrale du procès équitable : l’on est présumé innocent jusqu’à preuve du crime, et nul n’a à prouver son innocence. Il s’est aussi arrêté sur le droit au silence, s’interrogeant sur le sort d’une personne qui possède une fortune ou un avion et à qui l’on demande d’en expliquer l’origine, mais qui choisit de se taire : son silence ne peut valoir aveu ni preuve de culpabilité. Légiférer en matière pénale impose, a-t-il rappelé, de mobiliser toutes les garanties, tant la liberté et les droits sont en jeu. C’est dans ce cadre qu’il a exposé une piste à l’étude : un code autonome consacré à la lutte contre la corruption, qui sortirait ces infractions du Code pénal général pour réunir l’enrichissement illicite, le conflit d’intérêts, le blanchiment d’argent et les délits connexes, avec une procédure propre. L’objectif serait de concilier la fin de l’impunité et l’absence d’injustice. Côté méthode, Abdellatif Ouahbi a révélé avoir rassemblé les propositions déjà déposées par deux groupes parlementaires sur ces questions, et s’est dit prêt à y ajouter celles du PJD évoquées pendant la séance. Un rapport réunira les différentes visions et les problèmes juridiques soulevés. Son département est disposé à en débattre au sein de la commission parlementaire compétente et à bâtir collectivement une conception juridique qui combat la corruption tout en protégeant les droits des individus. L’enjeu, a-t-il insisté, est de lutter contre la corruption et de consolider l’État de droit, dont il a averti que le relâchement des garanties rendrait la restauration extrêmement ardue. Lutter contre la corruption exige, a-t-il conclu, de la précision et de l’intelligence juridique, tant dans la rédaction des textes que dans leur mise en œuvre. The post Corruption : Ouahbi promet trois lois et un procès équitable appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nigeria targets defence equipment self-sufficiency 61 years after DICON
items.description: ….DICON-D7G plans 7,000 jobs, seeks foreign investment, technology transfer By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nigeria’s drive towards self-sufficiency in military equipment production has received a boost, with DICON-D7G unveiling plans to expand indigenous defence manufacturing, attract foreign investment and create 7,000 jobs for retired military personnel and civilians. The initiative, being promoted at the ongoing Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) in Lagos, also includes plans to acquire about 40,000 square metres of land for an international defence exhibition centre. The Chief Executive Officer of DICON-D7G, Mr Osman Chennar, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday, saying the initiative was aimed at reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported military hardware through local production, technology transfer and industrial partnerships. DICON-D7G, a major sponsor of AFRIDEX, is using the exhibition to promote its vision of strengthening Nigeria’s military-industrial capacity through indigenous manufacturing, investment mobilisation and strategic partnerships. The initiative comes 61 years after the establishment of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON) in 1964, as the country continues efforts to develop the capacity to manufacture a significant proportion of the equipment required by its armed forces. Chennar said the organisation was working to bring government institutions, private investors, local manufacturers, research organisations and international technology partners together to expand Nigeria’s defence manufacturing capacity. “Our ambition is to move Nigeria from dependence on imported military equipment to a country that can increasingly manufacture, maintain and sustain its own defence requirements,” he said. He said the objective went beyond importing finished defence products, stressing the need to develop local capabilities in the design, production, maintenance and eventual export of military equipment. According to him, Nigeria has the human resources, technical expertise and industrial potential to achieve greater defence independence through strategic investments and effective partnerships. As part of its international expansion drive, Chennar said DICON-D7G recently participated in an exhibition in Qatar, where it explored partnerships with foreign manufacturers, investors and technology companies to facilitate technology transfer and strengthen local production. He described AFRIDEX as an important platform for connecting manufacturers, investors, technology developers and other stakeholders. On the proposed exhibition centre, Chennar said the organisation was seeking approximately 40,000 square metres of land in Lagos for a facility that would host international defence exhibitions, technology showcases, industrial trade fairs and investment forums. He said the centre would also serve as a commercial asset, generate revenue and provide Nigerian manufacturers with opportunities to showcase indigenous products to international markets. On employment generation, Chennar said the organisation was projecting 7,000 jobs, comprising 2,000 positions for retired military personnel and 5,000 for civilians. He explained that retired personnel would contribute their experience in engineering, training, logistics, administration and project management, while civilian employment would cover manufacturing, information technology, research, skilled trades and support services. Chennar further disclosed plans to expand manufacturing activities beyond arms and ammunition to include tanks, armoured personnel carriers, mine-resistant vehicles, boats and drones. The renewed ambition follows the signing of the DICON Amendment Act into law by President Bola Tinubu in November 2023, which provided an expanded framework for indigenous defence production. However, the plans will require sustained investment, research and development, technology transfer, quality assurance and effective collaboration between the public and private sectors to translate into increased domestic production. items.title: Raja Casablanca : Paco Jémez remercié après une évaluation des résultats sportifs
items.description: Le Raja de Casablanca a décidé de mettre un terme à sa collaboration avec son entraîneur espagnol Paco Jémez. Le club casablancais a officialisé cette décision ce lundi 2 novembre 2026, à travers un communiqué, à l'issue d'une évaluation de la situation sportive de son équipe première. Cette séparation intervient dans un contexte où les performances du Raja n'ont pas répondu aux attentes de la direction. Selon le communiqué du club, les résultats enregistrés, la qualité du jeu proposé ainsi que la progression globale de l'équipe sont jugés insuffisants au regard des objectifs fixés en début de saison. Après examen de la période écoulée, la commission sportive, en concertation avec la direction sportive, a estimé qu'un changement à la tête du staff technique était désormais nécessaire. L'objectif est d'insuffler une nouvelle dynamique au groupe et de relancer le projet sportif du club. Dans son communiqué, le Raja réaffirme sa volonté de poursuivre ses ambitions avec détermination et responsabilité, tout en soulignant son attachement à son histoire, à son statut et aux attentes de ses supporters. Le départ de Paco Jémez ouvre ainsi une nouvelle page pour les Verts, qui devront désormais trouver un nouvel encadrement technique capable de répondre aux exigences sportives du club et de renouer avec les ambitions affichées pour la saison 2026-2027. L'identité du prochain entraîneur appelé à prendre les commandes de l'équipe n'a pas encore été annoncée. items.title: At Kazakhstan forum, Pakistan presents Karachi and Gwadar ports as 'strategic gateways' for Central Asian trade
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan can serve as an important trade and transit corridor for the landlocked Central Asian countries, providing them with access to international maritime trade routes and global markets, Minister for Board of Investment (BoI) Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh said on Monday. He made the remarks while addressing the opening session of the Second Tianshan Forum for Central Asian Economic and Quality Investment, being held in Kazakhstan’s Almaty. The minister termed Pakistan’s three major seaports — Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar Port — “strategic gateways that could facilitate regional trade, strengthen transportation links and provide alternative routes for the movement of goods”, according to a press release by the BoI. Sheikh particularly underscored Karachi’s importance as Pakistan’s major industrial and commercial hub, noting that its established industrial base, business infrastructure, financial institutions and port facilities offered significant opportunities for trade, industrial partnerships and foreign investment. He also highlighted Gwadar’s potential to further strengthen regional connectivity and economic cooperation. Regional connectivity was “not merely about linking roads, ports and markets, but also about connecting economies, creating investment opportunities, generating employment and building shared prosperity across the region”, he remarked. The minister invited regional and international investors to explore opportunities in key sectors, including energy, infrastructure, logistics, transportation, manufacturing and trade. He emphasised that improved connectivity and reliable energy supplies were essential for unlocking the region’s economic potential, the BoI statement said. Highlighting the importance of regional cooperation, the minister acknowledged the contribution of the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation ( Carec ) Programme in promoting transport connectivity, facilitating trade and supporting economic integration among participating countries. He observed that Carec provided a valuable platform for strengthening economic partnerships between Pakistan and Central Asian states, the statement said. The minister emphasised that Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, youthful population, industrial capacity and seaport infrastructure positioned the country to play an important role in connecting Central Asian economies with international markets. The Second Tianshan Forum will conclude in Almaty on Tuesday under the theme “Strengthening Resilient Connectivity and Quality Investment in Central Asia”. According to information provided in its official agenda, the two-day forum is a follow-up to the success of the inaugural Tianshan Forum for Central Asia Economic Cooperation, and is aligned with the new Carec Institute Strategy 2026–2030, as well as the Carec 2030 Strategy Midterm Review Rolling Implementation Action Plan. “In 2026, the Carec region continues to face a highly uncertain external environment. Rising geopolitical tensions have raised energy and food prices, disrupted transport and logistics, and weakened the reliability of trade corridors,” the agenda said. At the same time, it added that intra-regional trade remained limited due to similar economic structures, weak production complementarities, and incomplete market opening. Persistent transport and logistics bottlenecks such as uneven infrastructure quality, fragmented asset management, and capacity mismatches kept trade costs high, it added. “Non-physical barriers, including inconsistent customs procedures, weak digitalisation, non-harmonised standards, and inefficient border operations, further constrain cross-border flows. Meanwhile, digital infrastructure — especially cloud services, data centres, and AI applications — is expanding rapidly and reshaping connectivity and competitiveness,” it said. It pointed out that Carec countries were progressing unevenly with “large gaps in backbone infrastructure, digital skills, and regulatory coherence”, calling for these gaps to be bridged to “effectively support inclusive growth, resilient connectivity, and regional integration”. Senior representatives from multilateral development banks, financial institutions, high-level policymakers, business leaders, local governments, and academia across the Carec countries are attending the forum to discuss policy and operational issues in strategic areas such as transport, trade, logistics, energy, and digital connectivity, and promote pragmatic, sustainable investment in the region.

items.title: Environnement : projets, financements et gestion des déchets au menu d’une table ronde à Conakry
items.description: Le ministère de l’Environnement et du Développement durable entend renforcer la coordination des interventions de ses partenaires techniques et financiers afin d’optimiser les ressources consacrées au secteur. Cette ambition était au cœur d’une table ronde organisée ce lundi 2 novembre 2026 à Conakry, qui a permis de faire le point sur les projets en cours, d’identifier les besoins de financement et d’examiner les moyens d’accompagner les priorités environnementales du pays dans le cadre de Simandou 2040 Dans son intervention, le ministre de l’Environnement et du Développement durable, Fassou Théa, a présenté les principales priorités de son département. Selon lui, la protection des ressources naturelles, la lutte contre les pollutions et l’adaptation aux changements climatiques constituent les principaux axes d’intervention du ministère. Le ministre a notamment insisté sur la nécessité de mieux protéger les forêts, les bassins versants et la biodiversité, tout en renforçant l’accès à l’eau et la préservation des moyens de subsistance des populations. Il a également souligné que les enjeux environnementaux et climatiques doivent être pris en compte dès la conception des investissements prévus dans le cadre de Simandou 2040. Parmi les actions prioritaires évoquées figurent la restauration du massif du Fouta-Djalon, la protection du bassin de Konkouré, la préservation des parcs et des zones humides, ainsi que le renforcement du contrôle des pollutions liées aux activités industrielles et minières. Fassou Théa a aussi évoqué la mise en œuvre des textes encadrant l’interdiction des plastiques à usage unique, le développement de solutions alternatives et la mobilisation de financements climatiques. Pour concrétiser ces ambitions, le ministre a sollicité l’accompagnement des partenaires dans la préparation des projets, les études de faisabilité, le renforcement des capacités et la mobilisation de financements adaptés. Il a proposé l’élaboration d’une feuille de route commune définissant les projets prioritaires, les responsabilités de chaque partie et un calendrier de suivi. Prenant la parole à son tour, le secrétaire général du ministère, Dr Karim Samoura, a expliqué que le cadre de concertation avec les partenaires avait été initié en 2023, avec notamment l’appui de l’Union européenne et de l’UNOPS. Il a indiqué que sa relance répond à deux préoccupations : recenser les projets réalisés, en cours et programmés au cours des dix dernières années, puis mieux coordonner les interventions, notamment dans la gestion des déchets plastiques. Selon lui, cette cartographie doit permettre d’identifier les zones insuffisamment couvertes et d’éviter les chevauchements entre projets. Il a cité l’exemple de la Haute-Guinée, confrontée à de fortes chaleurs et aux effets du changement climatique, mais qui bénéficie de moins de projets d’adaptation que d’autres zones. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité d’accompagner la mise en œuvre des mesures relatives à l’interdiction des plastiques à usage unique et d’intégrer les enjeux environnementaux, climatiques et de genre dans la planification des projets liés à Simandou 2040. Pour sa part, Marie Shand, chargée des questions environnementales à la Délégation de l’Union européenne en Guinée, a souligné l’importance de maintenir l’environnement au cœur du programme Simandou 2040, compte tenu de ses nombreuses implications. Elle a rappelé que les interventions des partenaires couvrent plusieurs domaines, notamment le climat, les forêts, le littoral, les océans, les plastiques et le marché carbone. Elle a ainsi plaidé pour une meilleure coordination afin de garantir la pertinence et l’impact des actions menées au bénéfice des communautés. Représentant la Banque mondiale, Keita Mamadi Kobélé a estimé que cette rencontre a permis d’harmoniser les points de vue sur les financements accordés au ministère et de dresser un aperçu des différentes interventions des partenaires. Il a salué un cadre d’échange favorable à une meilleure coordination et à un ciblage plus efficace des actions. Parmi les prochaines étapes, il a évoqué l’affinement de la matrice des activités et la tenue de rencontres périodiques entre les partenaires et le ministère afin de poursuivre les échanges et d’assurer un meilleur suivi des interventions. À l’issue de cette rencontre, le ministère et ses partenaires entendent poursuivre les échanges autour d’une meilleure répartition des interventions, d’un suivi régulier des projets et de la mobilisation des ressources nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des priorités environnementales du pays.

items.title: NUPRC opens bidding for 40 oil, gas blocks November 20
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) on Monday disclosed that bidding for 40 oil and gas blocks under the 2026 licensing round will commence on November 20, 2026. The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this at a roundtable discussion titled, ‘Energy Sovereignty in an Interconnected World: Aligning National Priorities, Markets and Global Security’, at the 2026 ADIPEC Exhibition and Conference in Abu Dhabi. In a statement by the Commission, Eyesan, who urged international investors to take advantage of Nigeria’s investment opportunities, said the country had become more competitive through improved security, attractive fiscal terms and incentives designed to reduce operating costs. She said: “We are expecting investors to turn to Nigeria. We are going in for another licensing round and we will be launching our bid portal on November 20. We expect to see interested investors because the environment is a lot more competitive. “We have set a very attractive fiscal framework for investors. The entire environment is a lot more secure. We have been able to manage costs with a lot of incentives for investors and we expect to see investors take up the offer when we open the portal.” The NUPRC chief executive attributed the improvement in Nigeria’s investment climate to the Petroleum Industry Act, PIA, enacted in 2021, as well as executive orders signed by President Bola Tinubu. She said the commission had conducted at least four successful licensing rounds between 2021 and 2026, attracting investments into the country’s oil and gas industry. According to her, this represents a departure from the pre-PIA era when licensing rounds were less frequent, adding that the reforms had strengthened Nigeria’s competitiveness in attracting upstream investments. On the country’s gas potential, Eyesan said Nigeria had an estimated 215 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves but was producing barely seven billion cubic feet per day, leaving significant opportunities for investors to develop the resource. She said recently completed and planned gas infrastructure projects would help unlock supplies, improve domestic availability and position Nigeria to serve regional and international markets. “The stars are already aligned. For gas infrastructure, we just completed very major infrastructure projects that will unlock gas supply in the country and the sub-region. We talk about two major projects on the drawing board to move gas through the Nigeria-Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline and Trans-Sahara Gas Pipeline. Again, this gas will go somewhere in Europe and will also meet regional demands. So, Nigeria is positioned to meet not just domestic supply,” she said. Eyesan noted that competition for investments had intensified globally, with more countries discovering petroleum resources and seeking to attract international capital. She said Nigeria had taken steps to address factors investors consider before committing funds, including execution risks, costs, project delays and policy uncertainty. According to her, the Commission was determined to minimise these risks and create an enabling environment for the investments required to develop the country’s vast oil and gas resources. “We understand that investors will prize execution risk, cost, delays and also uncertainty and so what we have done in Nigeria is to ensure that we guard against these risks and then attract the investment required to enable us unlock the huge resources we sit on,” the NUPRC boss stated. items.title: Finance Ministry approves 10 months’ arrears for Judicial Service staff amid JUSAG strike
items.description: The Ministry of Finance has approved the payment of ten months’ salary and allowance arrears for staff of the Judicial Service and members of the Lower Court Bench. The arrears, arising from the implementation of new conditions of service, will be paid in two instalments, with the first covering January to May 2026 and scheduled for payment in November. The second instalment, covering June to October 2026, is expected to be paid in December. In a letter dated November 2, 2026, and signed by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, the Ministry directed the Controller and Accountant-General to give effect to the approval. According to the Ministry, the new conditions of service were approved by the President pursuant to Article 149 of the 1992 Constitution and took effect on January 1, 2026. The approval comes amid an ongoing strike by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG), which has disrupted activities at several court premises across the country. The Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Accra Circuit Court and some District Court offices have been locked, with security personnel restricting access to the premises. Supreme Court announces sitting Despite the disruption, the Office of the Judicial Secretary has announced that the Supreme Court will convene for its normal court business on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A notice issued on Monday, November 2, said the sitting was directed by the Chief Justice to enable the Court to proceed with its scheduled business. The notice, signed by Judicial Secretary Musah Ahmed, informed lawyers and parties involved in proceedings before the Court of the arrangement. “Pursuant to the direction of His Lordship, the Chief Justice, it is hereby notified for the information of all Lawyers and parties to proceedings that the Supreme Court shall convene for its normal court business tomorrow, Tuesday, 3rd November 2026,” it stated. It further advised all counsel and parties with cases listed before the Court to take note of the arrangement and govern themselves accordingly. The Finance Ministry’s approval represents a significant development amid the industrial action. However, the letter does not indicate whether the payment arrangement addresses all the concerns raised by JUSAG or whether the association intends to suspend its strike.

items.title: PTI lawyer Salman Safdar says he met Imran, Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail
items.description: PTI lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday said he met with party founder Imran Khan and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail, where they are both incarcerated. Imran has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023 , while his wife was arrested on Jan 17, 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced. The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives , Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted in recent months. In a post on X on Monday, Safdar said the meeting was his first with Imran after seven months and with Bushra in 11 months. The last time he met Imran, the Supreme Court designated him as amicus. However, this time he met Imran Khan as his lawyer. It lasted 40 minutes and was “insufficient to cover all cases [and] legal matters”, the PTI counsel contended. “Both briefed me on their health conditions [and living] conditions and gave Fresh instructions for some legal matters and cases,” he wrote on X. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn that he spoke to Safdar in detail. “Salman told me that the meeting was held in connection with a number of applications which have been filed in courts to arrange meetings with Imran Khan,” he said. “Salman has told me that he reached Adiala Jail at around 4:30pm and the meeting continued for around 40 to 45 minutes. However, he said that it was not sufficient time for the meetings, as there were so many cases which had to be discussed and as the meeting was being held after such a long time.“ Replying to a question, Akram said that no political issues were discussed during the meeting, which he added was also attended by Bushra Bibi. Safdar spoke about the cases and asked about future strategy. When asked about Imran’s health, Akram replied that although health issues were discussed, the PTI would only speak about the legal cases. Barrister Safdar’s last publicly reported meeting with Imran was held on April 8 this year, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to arrange the meeting. His previous meeting on Feb 10 with the former premier was also on the directives of the Supreme Court, where concerns about Imran’s health were raised. Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. While he has undergone eye procedures at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), his family demands that he be shifted to a hospital of his choice. The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency on the matter, of not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and of not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations. Imran was sent to jail for a three-year term on Aug 5, 2023 for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts. However, he and Bushra are also serving a 14-year sentence in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case . The couple were convicted in another Toshakhana case in December 2025, with 10-year and seven-year terms handed to them. The PTI founder also faces pending trials in terrorism cases related to the May 9, 2023 riots . Imran’s sisters Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, along with opposition leaders, have staged frequent sit-ins outside the Adiala jail demanding the PTI founder’s release. They remain unable to stage more sit-ins since their detention in late September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

items.title: Sam George says over 3.1 million Ghanaians using virtual assets to come under regulation
items.description: Minister for Communications and Digital Technology, Samuel Nartey George, has disclosed that more than 3.1 million Ghanaians are using virtual assets, including cryptocurrencies. To this end, he has assured users that the government’s quest to regulate the sector is not intended to slow down innovation but to strengthen the ecosystem and safeguard its use. He was speaking at the maiden African Virtual Assets Summit, organised by the Securities and Exchange Commission. The Virtual Assets Summit is the first of its kind in Ghana since the promulgation of the Cybersecurity and Virtual Asset Bills, which are aimed at safeguarding the use of the digital financial ecosystem. In his keynote address, Minister for Communications and Digital Technology Samuel Nartey George defended the need to regulate the sector, noting that more than 3.1 million Ghanaians are using virtual assets. “Ghana will not stand on the sidelines to watch this change unfold; we will regulate it to make it safe for our people. The memorandum for the Virtual Assets and Services Providers Act, 2025, Act 1154, states that Ghana ranks 29th in the world for cryptocurrency adoption, with about 3.1 million Ghanaians using these assets. Activities on that scale cannot sit outside the law; they must be brought within the law, and that’s exactly what we have done in parliament by passing Act 1154,” he said. The Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson Asiamah, has said the use of virtual assets could support governments in finding solutions to the long-standing challenge of access to credit. Deputy Director-General of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Mensah Thompson, urged financial market regulators to be innovative as the virtual assets market becomes more sophisticated through the use of technology. Organised by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Ghana and its partners, the forum provided a platform for African regulators to deliberate on measures to move away from physical cash.

items.title: JOJ Dakar2026 : Quand le patriotisme des influenceurs est mis à l’épreuve
items.description: Le Sénégal a réussi l’ouverture historique des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, ce samedi 31 octobre, au stade Abdoulaye Wade. Une cérémonie riche en couleurs où le savoir-faire sénégalais a été mis en lumière, plaçant la culture au centre de cet événement. Ce succès a été salué à l’unanimité par la presse nationale et internationale, tandis que les réseaux sociaux s'enflammaient. La fibre patriotique a vibré, mais justement, sur la toile, l'attitude de certains créateurs de contenus et influenceurs a été pointée du doigt. Sur de nombreuses plateformes, des personnalités suivies par des communautés massives ont brillé par leur silence face à cet événement historique organisé pour la première fois en terre africaine, avec l’insigne honneur pour le Sénégal d'en être l'hôte. Nommés explicitement, certains influenceurs ont été ouvertement critiqués pour n'avoir ni participé à l'événement ni contribué à le faire connaître via leurs réseaux. Au moment où Dakar est l’épicentre du monde, et où de nombreux créateurs venus d'horizons divers se trouvent sur le sol sénégalais pour prouver que l'Afrique a la capacité d'organiser des compétitions d'envergure internationale, des figures locales ont été interpellées par leurs abonnés pour leur manque d'élan patriotique : « Ils se terrent quand il n'y a pas d'argent en jeu. » « Est-ce qu’ils ont été invités ? Ont-ils été contactés ? » Telles sont les questions qui ont ressurgi pour tenter de les défendre. Ces interrogations sont légitimes, OUI. Mais doit-on réellement attendre d’être impliqué officiellement lorsqu'il s'agit de la nation ? La République appelle, et le patriotisme voudrait que l’on soit en première ligne pour répondre présent et mettre son savoir-faire au service de son pays. Un simple post, une simple republication suffiraient à montrer à la face du monde que, OUI, l’Afrique est capable de rivaliser avec les plus grandes puissances lorsqu'il s'agit d'excellence et d'organisation. Fatou NGOM

items.title: SIAO 2026 : Le ministre Serge Gnaniodem Poda visite le village du pays invité d’honneur
items.description: L’ambassadeur du Ghana, Kenneth Akibate, a accueilli le ministre chargé de l’Artisanat, Serge Poda, au village du pays invité d’honneur. La 18 e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou accueille le Ghana comme pays invité d’honneur. A cet effet, un village leur a été exclusivement attribué. Le ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, y a fait un tour le lundi 2 novembre 2026. Il a été accueilli par l’ambassadeur du Ghana auprès du Burkina Faso, Kenneth Akibate, qui lui a présenté les différents produits exposés par son pays. Il a avoué avoir apprécié la visite du ministre car c’st une occasion pour échanger et montrer tout ce que le Ghana a au SIAO. « Comme nous sommes le même peuple, nous ne pouvons pas être ailleurs quand un tel événement se déroule au Burkina », a-t-il ajouté. Le responsable d’équipe, représentant la Ghana Export Promotion Authority, Seidu Saaka Bakari, a expliqué que le Ghana est présent avec plus de 100 exposants et exportateurs venus présenter des produits ghanéens. Le village est la vitrine de l’artisanat du Ghana au SIAO. « Il y a une grande variété de produits, allant de l’agroalimentaire à l’artisanat en passant par les tissus et bien d’autres articles. Nous avons beaucoup de produits exposés », a-t-il souligné. Il a en outre promis, qu’à son retour, de recommander à son pays de toujours bien préparer sa participation à ce salon. Selon lui, la plupart des exposants ghanéens sont très heureux d’être présents. Certains ne s’étaient pas inscrits au départ, mais ils ont entendu parler de l’événement plus tard et sont venus demander des stands, foi de Seidu Saaka Bakari. « Malheureusement, tous les stands sont déjà occupés. Nous essayons toutefois de trouver une solution pour accueillir certains d’entre eux à différents moments afin qu’ils puissent présenter leurs produits », a-t-il révélé. La Journée consacrée au pays invité d’honneur, le Ghana, a lieu ce mardi 3 novembre dans l’enceinte du SIAO. Wendyam Pascaline KALMOGO Crédit Photo : Edith BAKALA

items.title: Air Algérie lance une nouvelle promotion : tarifs et destinations concernées
items.description: La compagnie Air Algérie a lancé des promotions sur plusieurs destinations vers l’Europe et l’Afrique du Nord. L’offre promotionnelle, qui a débuté le 29 octobre et prend fin le 30 novembre prochain, concerne des billets aller/retour en classe économique. Un billet Alger-Londres (Heathrow) est proposé à partir de 55 064 dinars tandis qu’un Alger-Genève est accessible à partir de 38 810 dinars. Les billets en partance d’Alger vers Bruxelles, Lisbonne et Vienne sont proposés respectivement à partir de 39 696 dinars, 38 648 dinars et 34 341 dinars. Les clients de la compagnie Air Algérie peuvent aussi profiter des offres concernant Biskra-Lyon (proposé) à 35 500 dinars ou Tlemcen-Marseille à partir de 35 000 dinars ou encore Annaba-Istanbul à partir de 45 000 dinars. À destination des capitales nord-africaines, Air Algérie propose un Alger-Tunis à partir de 27 000 dinars et un billet Alger-Le Caire à partir de 53 000 dinars. Nouvelle promotion d’Air Algérie : la ligne Alger-Paris n’est pas concernée Les billets à destination de Paris, qui enregistrent habituellement une plus forte demande, ne sont pas concernés par cette offre promotionnelle. Un billet vers la capitale française depuis Alger est proposé au tarif normal à partir de 64 657 dinars et peut dépasser les 80 000 dinars, en fonction des dates choisies par les potentiels clients. Un billet Sétif-Lyon est accessible à partir de 55 209 dinars et peut dépasser 68 000 dinars durant ce mois de novembre. Vers l’Afrique, Air Algérie propose, pour le mois en cours, un billet Alger-Johannesburg à partir de 61 232 dinars en classe économique et à partir de 246 132 dinars en classe business. Un billet Alger-Abidjan en classe économique est accessible à partir de 72 350 dinars, contre 180 150 dinars en classe business. Le billet Alger-Addis-Abeba, à destination de la capitale éthiopienne, est proposé à 193 077 dinars en classe Affaires contre 99 435 dinars en classe économique. items.title: PDP expels two Gombe chieftains over anti-party activities
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has expelled two of its chieftains in Gombe State, Hon. Khamisu Ahmed Mailantarki and Hon. Usman Aliyu Garry, over alleged anti-party activities and gross misconduct. The decision means the two politicians have lost their membership of the party and all rights and privileges accruing to them, following disciplinary proceedings over alleged actions the PDP said were capable of bringing it into disrepute. The PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, announced the expulsion in a statement, saying it followed the findings of the party’s Disciplinary Committee and consideration by relevant party organs. According to the statement, the offences against the two members fell under Sections 58(1)(a), (b), (h) and (j) of the party’s 2017 amended constitution, covering misconduct and activities considered detrimental to the party. The party maintained that the disciplinary process complied with the right to fair hearing under Section 57(6) of its constitution and Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution. Invoking Section 59(1)(j) of its constitution, the PDP declared that Mailantarki and Garry had ceased to be members and would no longer enjoy any affiliation, rights or privileges within its structures. Reaffirming the supremacy of its constitution, the party warned that members’ status would not shield them from disciplinary action. “No member, regardless of status, is above the Party’s laws and disciplinary framework,” the PDP stated. The party also stressed that its constitution remained binding on every member, regardless of position or standing within its structures. “The Party reiterates that its Constitution remains supreme and binding on all members,” it added. The PDP urged its members to remain loyal, disciplined and committed to its ideals, while working collectively to strengthen the party at all levels.
